Mitford and A Petition of the several Persons whose Names are

poor Petition thereunto subscribed, being respectively Owners and Occupiers of Estates within the Hundreds of Mitford and Launditck, in the County of , was presented to

the House, and read; Setting forth, That in the Year 1775, an Act was passed for the better Relief and Employment of the Poor within the said Hundreds, by virtue of which the said Hundreds were incorporated, and Directors and Guardians were appointed and chosen, for the Purpose of carrying the Provisions of the said Act into Execution; part of a large House was erected for the Reception of the Poor of the said incorporated Hundreds, and a considerable Debt was incurred in building and furnishing the same; and that, in pursuance of the Directions of the said Act, a certain fixed Annual Payment, or Contribution, was charged upon each of the Parishes within the said incorporated Hundreds, for the Purpose of defraying the Expences incurred in.erecting the said House, and for the Support and Employment of the Poor maintained therein; and that the said Act has, under the Experience of upwards of Twenty Years, been found very inadequate to its pro-felfed Object, viz. the better Relief and Employment of the Poor; and that the average Annual Payments, imposed and fixed under the Authority of the said Act, upon the said respective Parishes, are in many Instances, and in a high degree, dilproportionate, to the manifest Injury of several of the said Parishes, numerous Instances of which the Petitioners are prepared to prove to the House; and that, in Addition to the Money originally borrowed, a further Debt to a considerable Amount has been unavoidably incurred, in the Support and Maintenance of the Poor of the said incorporated Hundreds, and the Annual Contributions imposed under the said Act are inadequate to the Purpose of keeping down the Interest of the Debt, and defraying the ordinary Expences of the House, and of supplying the Poor with temporary Relief out of the House; and that the said incorporated Hundreds comprize Fifty Parishes, many of which are large and populous; and, from various Errors and Defects in the present System of Management, established under the Authority of the said Act, the Situation of the poor Persons maintained in the said House is in many Respects improper, the Children brought up therein become of little or no Use to the Community, and the Condition of the labouring Poor, residing in the said Hundreds, and endeavouring to maintain themselves and their Families by their Labour, is rendered in many Respects miserable and wretched, no , Diicrimination being made between the worthy and industrious and the idle and profligate, nor any Encouragement held out to Perlevcrance in Habits of Sobriety and honed Industry; and that it is necessary some effectual Measures should be speedily taken to remedy the Inconveniences and Mischiefs already prevailing, and to provide for the further and better Relief, Support, and Management, of the Poor within the said incorporated Hundreds; and, for this Purpose, it is expedient that certain Parts of the said Act should be repealed, and other Regulations substituted instead thereof, and further and other Provision made for the better Relief, Support, and Management of the Poor within the said incorporated Hundreds: And therefore praying. That Vo l. 56.

Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for the Purposes aforesaid; and that the Petitioners may have such further and other Relief in the Premises, as the Nature and Circumstances of the same may require, and as to the House shall seem fit and proper.

A Petition of the Butchers, redding in the Town and Neighbourhood of Kingston upon Hull, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That an Act passed in the last Session, to repeal so much of an Act, passed in the 2d Year of King James the First, as prohibits the Use of Horse Hides in making Boots and Shoes, and for better preventing the Damage of Raw Hides and Skins in the Flaying thereof; and that the Petitioners conceive the Evil intended to be remedied by such Act, if any, is small, and appears to be more imaginary than real, inasmuch, as in all Cafeswhere any Hide or Skin happens to be cut or galhed in the Flaying, the Butchers, who are the Owners and Sellers thereof, arc the greatest, if not the only Sufferers, because it hitherto has been, and will continue to be, the Custom for the Tanners and Skinners to inspect the Hides before they purchase them, and, whenever any Damage has been done thereto, the Butchers are constantly obliged to take an inferior Price for them; it is therefore evident, that the Butchers are equally interested with, if not more so, than the Skinners and Tanners, in preventing the gaihing of 5

Hides; and that such Act, instead of increasing, is likely to diminish the Revenue, and the Quantity of Leather heretofore manufactured, because, from the very great Difficulty, if not Impossibility, in preventing the gaihing of Hides, and owing to the numerous Penalties incurred thereby, few Persons, if any, will now attempt to flay a fallen Bead, the Hide or Skin thereof in many Cafes not being equal in Value to the Penalties incurred by the Person flaying the fame; and, that by one Clause of the said Act, which prevents the flaying of a Bead below the Knee or Gambul, the Revenue particularly differs a Loss in the Duty upon Leather, at kail of Four Pence by every Beast, and a great Quantity of Leather is thereby also loft, which might be made highly useful in making Childrens', and the inner Soles of other Shoes; and that, from the Operations of this Act, Butchers in general are prevented from taking and employing Apprentices, who are essentially requisite in their Business, and particularly in the flaying of Beads, because, if not from their Inattention, yet certainly fromtheir Inexperience and want of Skill, they cannot avoid occasionally gaihing the Hides more or less; vet there is not, even in this Cafe, any Provision or Exception in Favour of the Butcher, so as to exempt him from the manift.ld Penalties that attach to him, notwithstanding he is most evidently the greated, if not the only, Sufferer; and that the said Act does not seem to be calculated to produce any public Good, and, from its numerous and heavy Penalties, is productive of much Litigation, and is fraught with aimed endless Trouble and Inconvenience to the Country Butchers, who, by many of its midaken Regulations, and from the Ignorance and Prejudices of the Inspectors appointed under it, and front being obliged to attend at inconvenient Hours, and didant Places of inspection, are greatly obdructed and impeded in the free Exercise of their Calling; and that such Act is also partial and oppressive to the Country Butchers, inasmuch as the Butchers in the Metropolis, and for Fifteen Miles round the Royal Exchange in London, are wholly exempt from any of its numerous Inconveniences and Penalties, although no solid Reason appears why they should not be equally subject: thereto with the Country Butchers; And therefore praying the House to take their same into Consideration, and to repeal the said Act; and that it will be ever the Study of the Petitioners to avoid as little as possible the gashing of Hides, and to endeavour always to merit the Approbation of the House, and the Community at large.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Magistrates, Town Council, and other Inhabitants of the Town of Thurso, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners have long suffered the greatest Inconveniency from the Want of a proper Harbour, and from having no proper Regulations for paving, lighting, and cleansing the Streets, and for carrying on other Improvements in the said Town of Thurso-, and that it would tend greatly to the Safety and Protection of Vessels navigating

the North Sea, to have a commodious Harbour at Thurso; and the same would also essentially contribute to the Improvement of the Fisheries on the Northern Coasts of the Kingdom, as well as promote, encourage, and extend the growing Trade and Manufactures of the said Towh and adjacent Country; and that it would also tend greatly to the Benefit, Comfort, and Safety of the Inhabitants of the said Town and Port, if the Streets and Lanes therein were properly paved, cleansed, and lighted, and if all Nuisances, Annoyances, and Obstructions in the same were removed, and Provision made for preventing the like for the future; and that, deeply impressed with the Importance of accomplishing such desirable Objects, the Petitioners have subscribed certain Sums of Money for making a Harbour at Thurso; and they, with the rest of the Inhabitants of the said Town, are willing to be subjected to the Payment of certain Rates, Assessments, and Duties, for maintaining the said Harbour, as well as for carrying on the other Improvements above-mentioned: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for the necessary Purposes aforesaid.

A Petition of the Mayor and Commonalty of the City of York,was presented to the House, and read;

Setting forth. That the Bridge called Ouse Bridge, over the River Ouse, in the City of York, is very ancient, and, by reason of the Form and Construction thereof, and of the Buildings erected upon and near thereto, is very narrow, inconvenient, and dangerous for the passing of Carriages, Horses, Cattle, and Foot Passengers, so that the free Passage thereof is frequently interrupted; and therefore it is necessary to take down and re-build, or widen and enlarge the same; and also to widen, raise, and render more commodious, several Streets, Lanes, or Ways, leading or near thereto; which are at [ relent narrow and incommodious, and to pUrchafe and takedown several Houses and Buildings for that Purpose; and that the Bridge called Fofs Bridge, over the leading from Fofsgate into Walmgate, in the said City, is also

narrow, incommodious, and dangerous to Passengers, Carriages, and Cattle, passing over the same; and Part of the Streets leading thereto, at each Eud thereof, are narrow, and much obstructed by Buildings; and it is necessary that the said Bridge should be widened, and the Streets or Avenues leading thereto, at each End thereof, made safe and commodious, by taking down Part of such Buildings, or otherwise; and that all the Bars, Pofterns, Gateways, or public Entrances into the said City, are narrow and inconvenient; and the Arches of Fome of them are so low or narrow, that public loaded Stage Waggons, and other Carriages, having occ 'fion to pass through the fame, cannot conveniently do so with Goods, Wares, Merchandize, Hay or Straw, which they are authorized and accuftcmed to carry, but are frequently obliged either to unload Part thereof, for the Purpose of passing into or through the said C.ty, and afterwards to reload the fame, or to adapt the loading of such Carriages to the said Entrances and Arches; and, by reason of the Narrowuefs of the said Entrances, many Persons have been hurt or injured, and Foot Passengers cannot lafely pass through the fame; and that the Towers, Turrets, Walls, and other Stone Works of the like Nature, in, or surrounding, and appertaining to the said City of York, which belong to, or are repaired by, the Mayor and Commonalty of the same City, are mostly of great Antiquity, and, by reason thereof, are becoming ruinous, and liable to fall into Decay, and cannot be repaired, maintained, kept up, and preserved in good Order and Condition, but at a great Annual Charge and Expence, and more than the said Mayor and Commonalty are able to sustain and pay, without great Loss and Inconvenience; and that the said Bars, Pofterns, Gateways, or Entrances, Towers, Turrets, Walls, and Works, are not necessary to be kept up or -preserved for any public Use or Purpose; but, if the said Mayor and Commonalty were empowered to take down and remove the same respectively, or such of them, or such Part thereof, from Time to Time, as may be found expedient; and to appropriate the Ground or Soil thereof, and to work up and ule, or sell and dispose of, the Stone and Materials of the said Bars, Pofterns, Gateways, or Entrances, Towers, Turrets, Walls, and Works, so to be taken down and removed, and to apply such Stone and Materials, or any Part thereof, or the Money arising from the Sale and Disposition of the fame, or such Portion thereof, as may be deemed expedient, in or towards the re-building, widening, or repairing, of the said Bridges, or either of them, or for other public Purposes within the said City, it would tend to the

A Petition of the Company of Proprietors of the Canal Navigation from Manchester to Bolton and to Bury, under their Corporate Seal, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That an Act was passed in the 31st Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from Manchester to or near Prejlo-lee Bridge, in the Township of Little Lever, and from thence, by one Branch, to or near the Town of Bolton, and, by another Branch, to or near the Town of and to Weddell Brook, in the Parish of Bury, all in the County Palatine of Lancaster, by virtue of which Act the Petitioners were authorized to raise and contribute among themselves the Sum of £.47,700,. for making and completing the said Canal with the necessary Works and Conveniencies, and also, if need required, to raise the further Sum of £.20,000 for the like Purpose; and that the Petitioners have proceeded to cut the said Canal pursuant to the Directions of the said Act, and have made great Progress towards the Completion thereof, and in the Execution of the same have expended not only the said Sum of £.47,700, but also the said Sum of £.20,000, both of which Sums have been raised among the Petitioners, under the Powers of the Act; and that the Petitioners have caused an Estimate to be made of the Expence of making navigable and completing the said Canal with proper Works and Conveniencies, by which it appears it will require the further Sum of £.50,000 to finish the fame, and pay the Debts incurred by the said Proprietors, and now owing from them; and that, at present, the Petitioners reap little Benefit for the Sums already expended, and the Public are deprived of the Advantages they ought to derive from the Use of the said Canal; and that the Petitioners are utterly unable to raise the said further Sum, so wanted as aforesaid, without the Aid of Parliament; and that it may be necessary also, in some Particulars, to alter and amend the said Act: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to authorize and enable the said Company to raise the further Sum of £.50,000, for the Purposes aforesaid, by such Ways and Means, and under such Provisions and Regulations, as the House shall think proper; and that, if necessary, the said Act may be altered and amended.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. Blackburne of . Mr. Stanley, &c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's 9

Chamber; and have Power to fend for Persons, Papers, and Records.

That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to straighten, divert, make, alter, amend, and maintain, the said Road from the said Inn called The Lamb Inn, otherwise Fletcher's in Sharpies

aforesaid, to or new Brindle Lane End, otherwise Stoole Lane End, in Hoghton aforesaid, and to erect Three principal Turnpikes upon the said intended new Road, between the said Place called The Lamb Inn, in Sharpies aforesaid, and Brindle Lane End aforesaid, or near the last mentioned Place, and also several side Bars on the Sides of the same Road, and that, with the Money arising therefrom, the said Road may be made, amended, and repaired.

Royal Ex- A Petition of the Governor, Sub-Governor, Deputy fufaifce Com Governor, and Directors of the Exchange Af-

jnny'sPcti- finance, for insuring Ships and Goods at Sea, or going twn* to Sea, and for lending Money upon Bottomrie, was

presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That, by virtue of an Act, made in the 6th and 7th Years of the Reign of King George the First, for the better securing certain Powers and Privileges intended to be granted by his Majesty by the Charter for Afturanee of Ships and Merchandizes at Sea, and for lending Money at Bottomrie, and for other Purposes therein mentioned, his said Majesty did, by his Letters Patent, under the Great Seal of Great Britain, bearing Date at Westmhifter the zid Day of June 1720, incorporate divers Persons therein named to be a Corporation for insuring Ships and Goods at Sea, or going to Sea, and for lending Money on Bottomrie, by the Name of 'The Royal Exchange , with Power for them,

and their Successors, to make such Assurance; and that, by the said Charter of Incorporation, the Petitioners are empowered only to allure Ships, Goods, and Merchandizes at Sea, or going to Sea; and that a very extensive Inland Navigation is now carried on in different Parts of the United Kingdom by means of Canals, and frequent Applications have been made to the said Corporation to insure the Vessels concerned in these Navigations, and the Property laden on board them, which they do not conceive the present Charter empowers them to do; and that the Petitioners conceive, that any additional Security which can be given to the extensive Intercourse between the different Parts of the United Kingdom will be of National Benefit: And therefore praying. That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to empower the said Corporation to insure any Vessel or Vessels concerned in Inland Navigation, and the Goods, Merchandizes, and Effects, laden therein.

' Owners and Proprietors of certain Fen Lands, and Low Grounds, lying within the Manor or Township of North Kyme, in the County of Lincoln, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That an Act was passed in the 28th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for more effectually draining and preserving certain Fen Lands and Low Grounds in the Manor or Township of North Kyme, in the county of ; and that,

by the said Act, certain Trustees were directed to be appointed, from Time to Time, to carry the same into Execution, and for that Purpose they were empowered to rate and tax all the said Lands and Grounds with such Sum of Money, not exceeding One Shilling per Acre, in any Year, as they should findrequisite; and, if the Money so raised should be found insufficient, then with such further Sum, not exceeding Six Pence per Acre, as they should be authorized to impose, by the Owners and Proprietors of the said Lands and Grounds, assembled at a Meeting to be held for that Purpose; and that the said Trustees have, from Time to Time, proceeded in the Execution of the said Act, and the Rates or Taxes aforesaid have been raised and applied in making and maintaining Works Of Drainage upon the said Lands and Grounds; but the said Rates or Taxes are found very insufficient to defray the Expence of properly draining and preserving the said Lands and Grounds, and for which Purpose it is also necessary that additional Works of Drainage should be made; and that it is re-quisite the said Act should be amended, and the Powers and Provisions thereof altered and enlarged; and particularly that further Rates or Taxes should be authorized to be laid: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to alter, amend, and render more eftcftual, the said Act, in such Manner as to the House shall leem meet.

Hallamshire,in the County of under their Corporate

Seal, and of the several Merchants, Manufacturers, and others, of the Town and Neighbourhood of Sheffield, interested in the Manufacture of Cutlery Wares, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, vfas presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the manufacturing and vending of Knives, Sickles, Shears, Sciffars, Razors, Files, and Forks, made of wrought or forged Iron, and Steel, is carried on at Sheffield, in afor'elaid,

and elsewhere, to a great Extent, and forms a very valuable and important Branch of the Manufactures and Commerce of this Kingdom, and by realon of the general Estimation and Repute to which such Cutlery Wares have been raised by their l'uperior Quality, great Quantities thereof are now annually exported into Foreign Countries; and that many of such wrought or forged Cutlery Wares, namely. Knives, Sciffars, Razors, and Forks, have, for some Time past, been imitated by the like Manufactures of Call Iron, made in Moulds, which Call Iron Manufactures are brittle and weak, and of an inferior Temper and Quality, but are now so well d re fled and polished, and bear so exaCl a Resemblance to the said wrought or forged Cutlery Wares, that a Stranger to the Business scarce can distinguish the one from the other without trying their Strength and Elasticity; and, for Want of some distinguishing Mark upon such Call Iron Wares, great Deceits and Frauds are, and may be, praCliled upon the Public in the vending thereof, and the said wrought or forged Cutlery Wares are in Danger of losing their Repute, and particularly in Foreign Markets; and that certain deceitful and fraudulent Practices have been, and may be, used by Persons marking or stamping upon Knives, Sickles, Shears, Seiffars. Razors, Files, and Forks, or some of them, " Call Steel,or Shear Steel," when such Goods are only common Steel; and that an Act was passed, in the 31st Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for the better Regulation and Government of the Company of Cutlers within the Liberty of 'Hallamshire aforesaid, and within Six Miles of the said Liberty, and of their Journeymen and Apprentices, some of the Provisions in which Act have been found inconvenient and ineffectual: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for regulating the making and vending of Call Iron Cutlery Wares, and for preventing the Purchasers of such Wares being deceived in the real Quality thereof; and for preventing Persons from striking or marking, upon any Cutlery Wares, any Word or Words, indicating the same to be of a l'uperior Quality to what they really are; and also for amending and rendering more effectual, the said Act of the 3 ill Year of the Reign of His present Majesty.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

celles. See.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to fend for Persons, Papers, and Records; and all who come to the Committee are to have Voices.

Durham, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners, with divers other Persons, were appointed by the said Act of the 28th Year of His present Majesty's Reign, Trustees for putting the same in Execution, and they have, by the Money arising from the Tolls, and borrowed on the Credit thereof, completed such Works as the said Act pre-feribes and directs to be carried into Effect, which, the Petitioners conceive, tend much to the Safety and Accommodation of the Public j and that the Money now remaining due on the Credit of the said Tolls amounts to the Sum of £. 8,000, and upwafds, and the Term created by the said Act will expire in the Year 1803, within which Period the Tolls collected by virtue thereof will not be sufficient to discharge the said Sum of £.8,000, and the Interest attending the fame; and that it will materially conduce to the further Convenience of the Public, if the Petitioners wrere empowered to add to the said Stone Bridge, by Means of additional Arches of Stone, projected from the Piers thereof, so as give to the same an increased Width of Twelve Feet, or thereabouts: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to enlarge the Powers of the said Act of the 28th Year of His present Majesty's Reign, and to continue the Tolls now collected and received by virtue thereof, for such further Term as will be necessary to raile Money sufficient to discharge the said Sum of £.8,000 so remaining due on the Credit of the said Tolls aforesaid, and the Interest thereof, and the Expence attending such additional Arches, and to answer the other Purposes of the said Act.

A Petition of Matthias Koops,of James Street, in the KooptHdent Parish of Saint Margaret, Westminster, in the County of Petitl0JU

Middlesex, Gentleman, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioner* after much Trouble, Labour, and Expence, hath discovered and invented a Mode of manufacturing Paper from Straw,

Hay, Thistles, Waste and Refuse of Hemp and Flax, and different Kinds of Wood and Bark, fit for printing, and other useful Purposes; in Consideration of which Invention His Majesty has been graciously pleased to grant unto the Petitioner Letters Patent, under the Great Seal of that Part of His Majesty's United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, Wales, and Town of Berwick upon Tweed, dated the 17th Day of February last, for the Term of Fourteen Years, with a Proviso contained in the said Letters Patent, that, if the Petitioner should not particularly describe and ascertain the Nature of his said Invention, and the Manner the same was to be performed, by an Instrument in Writing under his Hand and Seal, and cause the same to be inrolled in the Court of Chancery of that Part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called Great Britain, within Twelve Calendar Months next after the Date of the said Letters Patent, the said Letters Patent, and all the Liberties and Advantages thereby granted, should utterly cease, determine, and become void; and also a Proviso, that, if the Petitioner, his Executors or Administrators, or any Person or Persons which should or might at any Time or Times hereafter* during the Continuance of the said Grant, have or claim any Right, Title, or Interest, in Law or Equity, of, in, or to the Power, Privilege, and Authority, of the foie Ule and Benefit of the said Invention thereby granted*

should make any Transfer or Alignment, or any pretended Transferor Assignment, of the said Liberty and Privilege, or any Share or Shares of the Benefit or Profit thereof, or should declare any Trust thereof to of for any Number of Persons exceeding the Number of Five, or should open, or cause to be opened, any Book or Books for Public Subscriptions to be made by any Number of Persons exceeding the Number of Five, in order to the raising any Sum or Sums of Money under Pretence of carrying on the said Liberty or Privilege thereby granted, or should by him or themselves, or his or their Agents or Servants, receive any Sum or Sums of Money whatsoever of any Number of Persons, exceeding in the Whole the Number of Five, for such or the like Intents or Purposes, or should prelume to act as a Corporate Body, or should divide the Benefit of the said Letters Patent, or the Liberties and Privileges thereby granted, into any Number of Shares exceeding the -Number of Five, or should commit or do, or procure to be committed or done, any Act, Matter, or Thing* whatsoever, during such Time as such Person or Persons should have any Right or Title, either in Law or Equity, in or to the said Premises, which would be contrary to the true Intent and Meaning of an Act, made in the 6th Year of the Reign of King George the First, for the better securing certain Powers and Privileges intended to be granted by His Majesty by Two Charters for Assurance of Ships and Merchandizes at Sea, and for lending Money upon Bottomry, and for restraining several extravagant and unwarrantable Practices therein mentioned (or in case the said Power, Privilege, or Authority, should at any Time thereafter become veiled, or in Trust, for more than the Number of Five Persons* or their Representatives, at any one Time, reckoning Executors or Administrators, as and for the single Person whom they represent, as to such Interest as they were or should be entitled to, in Right of such their Testa-for or Intestate) that then, and in any of the said Cafes, the said Letters Patent, and all Liberties and Advantages whatsoever, thereby granted, should utterly cease, determine, and become void, any Thing therein contained to the contrary thereof in anywise notwithstanding i and that, in order to carry on the said Manufac-

Y y ture

ture of making Paper from the Substances before-mentioned with Efl'edl, and so as to render it beneficial and advantageous both to Government and the Public, as well as to the Petitioner, will require a large Sum of Money, far beyond the Means or Power of the Petitioner to bring forward or advance, but several Gentlemen of Property and Respectability have agreed to advance and hazard a large Capital in the establishing the said Manufacture, and carrying the same into Effect, on being permitted to become Partners or Shareholders in the fame, and, for the Purpose of establishing the fame, are ready to agree to build, in the Vicinity of London, a very large Manufactory, which, the Petitioner conceives, will be of great National Benefit, as it will increase the Revenue, employ numerous Hands, of both Sexes, and of all Ages, and prevent the Necessity of so much Money being sent to the Continent for the Purchase of Rags, as also increase the Value of Lands, and ultimately reduce the Price of Paper, and, in the Course of Time, enable Government, without injuring the Trade, to reduce the Drawback now paid to the Exporters of Paper, as Paper manufactured from Straw, Hay, and other Vegetable Substances, might be sold at a cheaper Rate for Use on the Continent, than they now are able to manufacture it from Rags; but the Petitioner is unable to accede to l'uch Proposal, in consequence of the last mentioned Proviso contained in the said Letters Patent; and that the Petitioner has also prepared a particular Description of his said Invention and Discovery, pursuant to the Proviso contained in the said Letters Patent, and, in order that the true Intent and Meaning of the said Proviso may be complied with, and the full Benefit of the said Invention may be secured to all His Majesty's Subjects . at the Expiration of the said Term of Fourteen Years; but he is informed, that, if the said Invention be inrolled in the said Court of Chancery, there is no Means of preventing Copies thereof from being obtained by Foreigners and others, who will thereby have the Advantage over His Majesty's Subjects, in as much as they will be enabled to make Use of the Petitioner's said Invention and Discovery in neighbouring Countries, and more especially in France, which exports large Quantities of Paper for Paper Hanging to America, previous to the Expiration of the Term of the said Letters Patent, to the manifest Injury of the Petitioner, who might otherwise supply those Countries with Paper, for the Reasons before stated, during the said Term, and to the Disadvantage of the Trade of this Kingdom, which would otherwise be very much benefited by his said Invention; and that the Petitioner is also soliciting, and has Reasons to believe he shall obtain, Letters Patent for that Part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, called Ireland, as also for that Part of Great Britain called

Scotland j and that the Petitioner conceives it will be expedient, for the Reasons above stated, that the said particular Description so prepared by him, instead of being inrolled in the Court of Chancery of that Part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called Great Britain, and as may be directed by the said Letters Patent now soliciting for those Parts of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called Ireland, and that Part of the Kingdom of Great Britain called Scotland, and consequently made accessible to improper Persons, should be delivered within the said limited Time to such principal Officers of the Courts of Chancery and Chancellary of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, as may be thought proper for their Inspection and Satisfaction, as to the Sufficiency of such Description or Specification, and that the same should be kept under their Seals, to be resorted to by the said Officers on all necessary Occasions, without being open to the Inspection of Foreigners and others: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill, for authorizing such Delivery of the said particular Descrip-4

tion or Specification within the said limited Time, instead of the same being inrolled in the said Courts of Chancery and Chancellary; and, that for effectually securing to the Petitioner, and the Public, the Benefit and Advantages of the said Invention and Discovery, and enabling the Petitioner to carry the same into Effect, the said Letters Patent, and the Liberties and Advantages thereby granted, may be extended to such Number of Persons, and in such Shares and Proportions, as may answer the Purposes before-mentioned; or that the Petitioner may have such other Relief in the Premises, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Sir William Elford, Mr. Adams, &c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber j and have Power to fend for Persons, Papers, and Records; and all who come to the Committee are to have Voices.

That several Acts have been palfed for preserving, enlarging, and improving, the

S

said Harbour, and Trustees Were appointed for carrying the said Acts into Execution, and they were authorized to collect tcertain Rates and Duties for that Purpose laid upon Coals and Merchandize imported and exported at, and Shipping using, the said Harbour;, and that the Trustees proceeded in the Execution of the Trust reposed in them, and from Time to Time borrowed several considerable Sums of Money on the Credit of the said Rates and Duties, but the said Harbour being improved, they were enabled to pay off a great Part of the Debt they had contracted as aforesaid, and a large Sum of Money still remained in their Hands; and that, in the Year 1798, a voluntary Contribution being set on foot for the Aid and Assistance of Government, towards carrying on the War against the Enemies of Great Britain, the Trustees thought themselves authorized to pay out of the Money then in their Hands the Sum of £. 2,000to such Subscription; but Doubts have since been suggested, whether they had Authority so to apply that Money, the Petitioners, however, hope, that this House will think the Trustees, who directed such Application of the Money for so good and laudable a Purpose, should be indemnified for having so done; and that some Doubts have aril'cn on the Validity of the Elections of the Trustees between the Year 1710 and the Year 1796, and it is expedient such Doubts should be removed, and the Mode of appointing Trustees in future clearly ascertained; and that the said Acts also require Amendments, and Alterations, and Additions: And therefore praying.

That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for effecting the Purposes aforesaid, in such Manner as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

A Petition of the Mayor, Aldermen, and Common Council, of the Borough o Boston, in the County of Lincoln, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Bridge over the River , in the said Borough, is much too narrow, and, at present, in a very decayed and ruinous State and Condition, and is become inconvenient and dangerous to Passengers, Carriages, and Cattle, passing over the fame; and therefore it is necessary to take down and re-build the said Bridge, and all'o to widen, raise, and render more commodious, several Streets, Lanes, or Ways, leading or near thereto, and to purchase and take down several Houses and Buildings for that Purpose; and that the Situation of the present Bridge is very inconvenient and incommodious, and it will tend greatly to the Improvement of the Borough, if the intended Bridge was made and erected in a more proper and convenient Situation, very near the present Bridge, and, in such Calc, it will be necessary to purchase and take down several Houses and Buildings; and that the Gaol and House of Correction of the said Borough is, at present, in a very decayed and ruinous State and Condition, and by reason of the confined Situation thereof, and for Want of a free Circulation of Air, the same is become very unhealthy, and dangerous to the Lives of the Persons confined therein; and it is highly necessary that the said Gaol and House of Correction should be enlarged, and a proper and suitable Prison Yard added thereto, and for that Purpose it will be necessary to purchase and take down several Houses and Buildings and that the Market Cross of the said Borough, and several of the Rooms over the fame, which are appropriated for the Transaction of public Business within the said Borough, are toofmall, and at present very inconvenient and incommodious, and it is become necessary that the said Market Cross and Rooms should be enlarged, and made more convenient to Persons resorting thereto, or having Occasion to use the fame: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for effecting the several Purposes aforesaid, by such Ways and Means, in such Manner, and under such Restrictions and Regulations, as to the House shall seem meet.

A Petition of John Edwards, on Behalf of himself, and of Thomas Michel/and John TrevenSmelters and Refiners

of Copper Ores, at Hayle J\n the County of Cornwall, under the Name of The Cornish Copper Company, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the River and Harbour of Hayle, in the County of Cornwall, is much frequented by Ships and Vessels employed in the Conveyance of Copper Ore and other Merchandize to different Parts , of the Kingdom, and the Petitioners have, at their Expence, for several Years, expended corr-siderable Sums of Money in clearing and deepening the said River and Harbour, and have so far succeeded as to render the same more same and convenient for such Ships and Vessels, by erecting Flood Gates, and by making a Mound, Bank, or Jettce, near the Mouth of the River; but that further and other Works are necessary to complete the same, and it is proposed to increase and lengthen the said Jettee, to, or near, Low Water Mark, a Distance of about 5,000 Feet, which would not only concur in clearing out the Sand and deepening the Entrance, but afford a much greater Space for the Reception and safe lying of Ships, until they shall have Water, to the Places of taking in or delivering their Cargoes; and that, in order to make the said Harbour more l'afe and commodious for Ships and Vessels using the fame, it is expedient that Powers should be granted to complete the Works, and to reimburse to the Petitioners the Expences that shall be incurred in the doing thereof, for which Purpose it will be necessary to collect: a small Sum by Way of Tonnage, on such Ships and Vessels as shall hereafter enter the said River: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for effecting the Purposes before-mentioned, in such Manner, and under such Regulations and Restrictions, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

licence Pilots, for the piloting and conducting Ships and; Vessels into, and out of, the said Creek or Haven of Holy

A Petition of the Lord Provost, Magistrates, and Town Council, of the City of Glasgow, for themselves, and on Behalf of the Community of the said City, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the said City of Glasgow, within these last Fifty Years, has greatly increased in Size and Population, whereby the Duties of Magistracy, particularly of the Baillies, which consist in preserving the Peace and good Order, and superintending the Police of the City, and in administering Justice to the Inhabitants, have become so laborious, that it is almost impracticable for the present Baillies (who are only Three in Number) to perform those Duties to their own and the public Satisfaction, which renders an Addition to their Number necessary; and that the Fines, leviable from Persons refusing to accept the Offices of Lord Provost, Baillies, Dean of Guild, Conveener of the Trades, Treasurer and Councillors (owing to the Increase of Wealth, and Decrease of the Value of Money, since 1748, when those Fines were established), are not sufficiently compulfatory to secure the Acceptance of those Offices by the Persons chosen; and that, if the Number of Baillies be increased, it will be proper and expedient also to make an Addition to the ordinary Members of Council, so as to preserve the Number of Thirteen ordinary Councillors of the Merchant, and Twelve ordinary Councillors of the Trades Rank, over and above the Lord Provost and Baillies, and those Persons who are Councillors ex officiis-, and that the present Mode of electing Magistrates, and some of the other Office Bearers of the City, by dividing the Council into certain Lifts or Leets, has been found, by Experience, to be attended with considerable Difficulty and Inconvenience; and that there are Jikewife several other Parts of the Set or Constitution of the said City, relative to the Election of Office Bearers, and to their Situation after they are elected, which require Explanation

That the Road through the said County, from the High Bridge of Cree, by Nezvton Douglas, and Gknluce,to Portpalrick, and from thence by

Stranraer, to the Confines of the County of near the Cavin of Lochryan,being one of the great Communica-

tions between "England, Scotland, and Ireland, is in bad Repair, and cannot be properly amended, and kept in Repair, without the Aid of Parliament. — And the said Member further informed Your Committee, That the Laws now subsisting for the making of Roads and building Bridges in the said County, have been found inadequate; and, in order to render the same more effectual, it would be ui'cful and advantageous, that the Statute Labour of the said County should be converted into Money, and the Rates and Mode of levying the same ascertained, and some additional Assessment allowed to be imposed.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Mr. James Barnes, an Engineer, being examined, said,

Mr. Thomas Homer, Auditor to the said Company, being examined, laid. Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That His Majesty's Forest of South, alias East Bere, alias Bier, contains 1.3,000 Acres, or thereabouts, and the Soil of the said Forest is particularly well adapted for the Growth of Oak Timber, and is situate very conveniently for Communication with the Naval Yard at Portsmouth, being in most Parts contiguous thereto; and that the said Forest comprizesTwo Walks, called East and West Walks, which contain Eighteen several lmaller Districts, distinguished as Purlieus, Two of which belong to His Majesty, in Right of His Crown, and the remaining Sixteen belong to the Petitioners, and others, having Estates within the Regard of the said Forest; and that the said Forest, in its present State, yields very little Profit, either to His Majesty, or to the said Purlieu Owners, in Comparison of what it might do if the same was Disafforested, and divided, allotted, inclosed, and held in Severalty, by H is said Majesty, and the said several Persons interested therein as aforesaid; and that it hath been proposed, that a certain Portion of the said Forest shall be let out and allotted to His Majesty, His Heirs and Suc-cefi'ors, in Severalty, in lieu of His Rights in and over the said Forest, and as a Compenl'ation for the Dif-afforeftation of the lame, and for the Purpose of pre-lerving the Growth of Wood and Timber for the Supply of the Navy; that a certain other Part of the said Forest shall be set out and allotted to the said Robert Thistlet/nvayte, as Lord Warden as aforesaid, in lieu of his Rights in the said Forest; and that certain other Parts shall be set out and allotted to the Owners of Tythes arising within the said Forest, in lieu thereof; and that the Residue of the said Forest shall be set out and allotted to His Majesty, the Petitioners, and the other Purlieu Owners, and those Persons who have Right of Common and Turbary in the said Forest, according to their several Rights and interests therein, freed and discharged from all Tythes and other Claims whatsoever; and that such Division and Inclosure of the said Forest will not only tend to the Benefit of His Majesty, and all Persons interested therein, but, by reason of the Extent of the fame, and the general Richness and Fertility of the Soil, and its Vicinity to the Town of Vo 1. 56.

Portsmouth, will also be of great public Utility: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for dividing, allotting, and inclosing, the said Forest, under such Regulations and Restrictions, as to the House shall seem meet.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names Petition of are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of themselves, and others, interested in an intended Manufactory, to be pany. called " The Regenerating Paper Company," was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That Matthias Koops being in Possession of a Discovery or Invention for extracting Printing and Writing Ink from Printed and Written Paper, and converting the Paper from

which

which the Ink is extracted into Pulp, and making thereof Paper fit for Writing, Printing, and other Purposes, and for the foie and exclusive Exercise of which pifcovery or Invention within that Part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, Wales, and Town of Berwick upon Tweed, as also Scotland, for the Term of Fourteen Years, His Majesty has been graciously pleased to grant His Letters Patent unto the said Matthias Koops, his Executors, Administrators, and Assigns, dated respectively the 28th Day of April and the 17th Day of last; and which said Discovery the Petitioners conceive, from the present Scarcity of Rags, and consequent enormous Advance in the Price of Paper, is deserving of the Countenance and Support of the House; and that the Petitioners are desirous of carrying the said Invention and Discovery into Effect, by establishing Manufactories for that Purpose, but that such Manufactories cannot be established without great Rifkin the Undertaking, and without a very large Expence, nor can be conveniently carried on, unless a considerable joint Stock is raised for that Purpose; and that the Petitioners submit, that the establishing and carrying into Effect such a Manufactory is the most desirable, as every Year renders the Difficulty of obtaining Paper of all Descriptions greater, and it is much to be apprehended, that, if this Invention should not be so far encouraged as to be prosecuted with Effect, the Business of Printing, and particularly that of Newspapers, mull be in a great Degree discontinued, the Exportation of Paper be totally annihilated, and of course the Revenue suffer a considerable Diminution, unless some other Substitute to use for a Raw Material can be resorted to; and that the Petitioners further submit, that, in case the said Manufacture shall be established and carried into Effect, the Waste Paper which is now bought up by Grocers, Tobacconists, Cheesemongers, and others, will be re-tnanufactured, and those Persons obliged to consume coarse new-manufactured Paper, which will of Necessity greatly increase the public Revenue; and that the Petitioners, and several other Persons, have already agreed to form themselves into a Society, and to raise a Capital Stock of £.25,000, for the Purpose of establishing and carrying on the said Manufactory; but the Petitioners, and the other Persons who have agreed to subscribe and raise the said Capital Stock of £.25,000, for the Purpose aforesaid, are apprehensive that, under the re-strictive Provisoes contained in the said Letters Patent, no more than Five Persons can carry on the said Manufactory, or be jointly interested therein, without Forfeiture of the Liberties and Advantages guaranteed by the said Letters Patent; and that great Difficulties may arise, as well in recovering Debts, which may grow due to the Proprietors of the said Manufactory, as also in defending Suits or Actions which may be commenced or brought against the said Proprietors for any Matter or Thing relative to the said Manufactory, as, by Law, all the several Proprietors and Subscribers to the said Manufactory must in such same both sue, and be sued, implead, and be impleaded, by their several and dif-tinct Names and Descriptions: And therefore praying. That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to incorporate certain Persons therein named, and their Successors, and to extend to them the Rights, Privileges, and Advantages, contained in the said respective Letters Patent granted by His Majesty to the said Matthias Koops, as aforesaid; and also giving proper Powers

for the Purpose of establishing one or more Manufactory, or Manufactories, within that Part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called Great Britain, for the Purpose of extracting Printing and Writing Ink from Printed and Written Paper, and converting the Paper from which the Ink is extracted into Pulp, and for making thereof Paper fit for Writing, Printing, and other Purposes; and for the more effectually supporting and conducting the fame, in such Vol. 56.

A Petition of the Lord Provost, Magistrates, and Town Council, of the City of for themselves,

and on Behalf of the Community of the said City, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That by an Act, passed in the 12th Year of His present Majesty, for deepening, cleansing, scouring, preserving, and maintaining, the Harbour of Port for en-

larging and improving the Quays and Piers, for erecting new Breasts, Jettees, and Piers, and for regulating Ships, Lighters, and other Vessels, trading into, and going out of, the said Harbour, and for other Purposes therein mentioned, the Trustees named and appointed by the said Act, were empowered to levy certain Harbour Duties upon all Ships, Vessels, Barks, Lighters, and Boats, bound outward from, and coming into, the said Port or Harbour, for the Voyages described in the said Act, for the Purposes therein specified; and also to borrow, under the Authority of the said Act, any Sum or Sums of Money, not exceeding at any one Time the Sum of £.5,000 Sterling, upon the Security of the several Rates, Duties, and Tonnage, given and granted by the said Act, which Money so borrowed should be employed for the Ends and Purposes of the said Act, and not otherwise; and that the Petitioners, by virtue of the said Act, have advanced or borrowed nearly to the Amount of the said Sum of £.5,000, which has been applied for the Purposes specified in the Act, the Expenditure of which has been attended with the most beneficial Consequences to the Trade of the said City of Glasgow, and Town of Port Glasgow-, and that the Funds arising from she Duties authorized by the said Act have been found, from Experience, to be inadequate to the Purposes for which, they were intended, insomuch, that the Debt due to the Petitioners for executing the said Act has been gradually increasing for many Years, and is likely to continue to do so, to the great Loss of the Petitioners, and to the Injury of the said Trade, unless the said Funds be increased, by adding to the said Harbour Duties; and that, notwithstanding the Improvements which have been made under Authority of the said Act, yet Hill there is a very great want of Accommodation for the Ships and Vessels retorting to the said Harbour, owing to the small Extent of Docks and Harbours, and likewise great Inconvenience has arisen to the Merchants and Ship Owners for want of Ware-houses for Rowing their Goods and Commodities, which render additional Quays, Piers, Jettees, Wharfs, Docks, and other Accommodations to the said Harbour, and the Erection of additional Warehouses and Storehouses, absolutely necessary for the Trade of the said City and Town; and that these Accommodations and Conveniencies cannot be obtained without great additional Expence, which the Petitioners are willing to defray, upon Condition of their being authorized by Parliament to borrow such an additional Sum upon the Security of the said former and increased Harbour Duties, as may be necessary for carrying the intended Improvements fully into Elfedt; the Petition of the several Persons, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of themfclifesand others, Owners and Proprietors of certain Fen Lands, within the Manors and Parishes of Upwell and Outwell, and the Parishes of Denver and Welney, in the Ille of Ely, and Counties of Cambridge and Norfolk, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Bills o( Drainage, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth;

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Two Acts, palfed in the 22d Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, and the 13th Year of His present Majesty, for draining and improving certain Fen Lands within the Manor and Parishes of Upwell and Outwell, and in the Parishes of Denver and Welney, in Voj.. 56.

the Ille of Ely, and Counties of Cambridge and Norfolk, were read: And,

Mr. Thomas Holman being examined, said. That the Commissioners appointed by the said Acts, have proceeded in the Execution thereof, and have borrowed several Sums of Money upon the Security of the several Rates and Taxes authorized to be levied; which still remain due upon the Credit thereof, and have also incurred several Debts in executing the several Works of Drainage, which are ilill incomplete: That the said Fen Lands, containing in the whole near 11,000 Acres, might be further greatly improved by additional Works of Drainage, but the said Rates and Taxes are not sufficient for the Payment of the Interest of the Monies already borrowed, and for maintaining and keeping in Repair the present Works; and the several Powers given by the said Acts, are found defective and insufficient for the effectual Drainage of the said Fen Lands, and it is therefore expedient that the said Acts should be repealed, and further and other Powers granted instead thereof.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for more effectually draining and improving certain Fen Lands within the Manors and Parishes of Upwell and Outwell, and in the Parishes of Denver and Welney, in the Me of Ely, and Counties of Cambridge and Norfolk: And that Mr. AJlley and Sir Martin Browne Folkes do prepare, and bring in, t,he fame.

A Petition of the Common Brewers of the City of London, and the Parts adjacent, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That, by an Act, made in the 22d Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, apparently for the Purpose of encouraging the Brewing of good Table Beer, intituled, "An Act for repealing the Duties " payable for Beer and Ale above Six Shillings a Barrel; " exclusive of the Duties of Excise, and not exceeding " Eleven Shillings a Barrel, exclusive of such Duties,'* it was enacted, that, from and after the 5th Day of July 1782, the several Rates and Duties then payable for Beer or Ale above 6 s. the Barrel, exclusive of the Duties of Excise, and not exceeding iij. the Barrel, exclusive of such Duties, commonly called Table Beer, which should at any Time or Times be brewed by the Common Brewers in England and Wales, should cease and determine, and be no longer paid and payable, and in lieu and instead thereof there should thenceforth be raised, levied, collected, and paid, throughout England and Wales, for every Barrel of Beer or Ale above 6 s. the Barrel, exclusive of the Duties of Excise, and not exceeding nr. exclusive of such Duties, commonly called Table Beer, brewed by the Common Brewer, and so proportionably for a greater or Idler Quantity, the Sum of 3J. to be paid by such Common Brewer; and that* by another Act, made in the 33d Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, it was enabled, that, from and after the parting of that Act, it should and might be lawful to and for all Common Brewers in England and Wales to brew Beer or Ale above 6 s. the Barrel, exclusive of the Duty of Excise by Law imposed for, or in respect of, such Beer, and not exceeding 135. the Barrel, exclusive of such Duty, commonly called Table Beer, under, according, and subject to, the Rules, Regulations, Restrictions, and Provisions, which arc contained, provided, settled, or established, in and by the said Act, made in the 22tl Year of the Reign aforesaid, for Common Brewers brewing Beer or Ale above 6 s. the Barrel, exclusive of the Duties of Excise, and not exceeding 11 s. the Barrel, exclusive of such Duties, commonly called Table Beer; and such Common Brewers, so brewing such Beer or Ale above 6 s.the Barrel, and not exceeding 13 j. the Barrel, should not be chargeable with, or liable to pay for or in rel'pect thereof, any greater or higher Duty than was imposed by Law for or in rel'pect of Beer

or Ale above 6 s. the Barrel, exclusive of the Duty of Excise, and not exceeding 11 the Barrel, exclusive of such Duty, brewed as aforesaid; and that, since the passing of the last-recited Act, it has proved that a Price of 13 s.per Barrel, exclusive of the Duty, is not sufficient to support its Expences, to stand against the common Contingencies of Trade, and afford even a moderate Profit to the Brewer, so that the Brewers of Table Beer have, for a long Time pad, been labouring under great Difficulties, which have gradually increased, and are now become insupportable, owing to the extraordinary high Price of Malt and Hops, which, together with Pro-vender, Fuel, and Labour, have advanced, since the passing the said last mentioned Act, beyond all probable Computation, to which mud be added the increased Capital of a Brewer, arising from the great Advance of the Price of Calks and other Utensils; and that, in consequence, the Trade is now become altogether inadequate to its Expenditure; and that the Petitioners are deterred from endeavouring to alleviate these Grievances by brewing their Liquor of an inferior Quality, being aware that such a Measure would not only draw on them the Complaint of their Customers, but likewise occasion a still more heavy Loss by the Return of their Liquor, as is the Usage of the Trade; and that many of the Petitioners Customers have requested to be supplied with good Table Beer, for which they are willing to pay a higher Price, but this the Petitioners are retrained from legally doing by the before-mentioned Act, by virtue of which such Beer would become subject to the Strong Beer Duty of 8 s. per Barrel: And therefore praying the House, to take the Premises into Consideration, and That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to alter the Provisions of the said last mentioned Act, in such Manner, that Common Brewers may be authorized to fell Table Beer of a Price of 17 per Barrel, exclusive of the Duty, to such Persons as may choose to have it of that Quality; or that the Petitioners may have such other Relief as to the House shall seem meet.

A Petition of the President and Members of the Board of Agriculture, being offered to be presented to the House;

The Lord Hawkesbury (by His Majesty's Command)

acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That His Majesty having been graciously pleased, in consequence of an Address of the House, to constitute, by Letters Patent under the Great Seal, a Board of Agriculture for promoting the internal Improvement of the Country, the Petitioners beg Leave to acquaint the House, that the important Purposes intended by that Institution are carrying on, and are likely to be attended with beneficial Effects to the Public: And therefore praying, That they may be supported by a Grant for the present Year, to such an Amount, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of lundry Noblemen, Gentlemen, and others, Subscribers to an Institution, called The Veterinary Coll-'ge,being offered to be presented to the

House;

The Lord Hawkesbury (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth. That, in pursuance of the Plan stated to the House in a Petition by them presented on the 6th of February 1795, their Exertions have been continued to carry into Effect the several beneficial Purposes proposed to be derived from the Establishment of a College for the Study and Practice of Veterinary Science; that, for the general Benefit of the Proprietors of Horses, and other valuable Cattle, they have Pleasure in stating, that 93 Pupils have passed Examination at the said College, many of whom are now settled in different Towns of the Kingdom, and are practising the Knowledge they have acquired, to the great Advantage of the Public; and it is with peculiar Satisfaction the Petitioners are enabled to state, that the Importance of the In-ftitution having been taken into Consideration by His Royal Highness the Commander in Chief, the Propriety of appointing Persons, educated at the College, to be Veterinary Surgeons in the several Regiments of Cavalry, has been determined on, in pursuance of a Report from a Board of General Officers, to whom the Subject had been referred, and that, in consequence of such Decision, 34 Pupils, whose Education has been completed, are engaged in the Service of the Army, and 28 other Pupils are now pursuing the Studies at the College, several of them intending to fill similar Situations, as soon as they shall be deemed duly qualified, each of them being subject to the same rigorous Examination of the Medical Committee, and to be certified in the same Manner as has hitherto been practised in respect of the other Pupils of the College; and that the Petitioners further state, that, desirous of rendering, to the utmost of their Power, their Institution advantageous to the public Service, the Colonels of the different Cavalry Regiments have been invited to fend each a Farrier to the College, in order to his being taught the Structure, Economy, and different Diseases of the Horses Foot, and instrufted in a Mode of Shoeing, tending very materially to its Preservation; and that many Army Farriers have been consequently admitted into the College for Instruction in that particular Part of Veterinary Knowledge; and that the College continues under the Direction of the Professor Mr. Coleman, a Gentleman of Talents and Skill, and who, by many useful and important Discoveries in the Science, has, in the Opinion of the Petitioners, fully justified the Expectations formed of its Improvement, from his Exertions; and that the Petitioners have already stated to the House, the Difficulties which have occurred in the Execution of their Plan, and particularly from the embarrassed State of their Finances; and, though the Aid so liberally granted by Parliament, has, in a great Degree, alleviated their Difficulties, it has yet proved inadequate to remove them entirely, notwith-standing the Petitioners have, with the utmost Frugality, reduced their Annual Expenditure much within the Estimate of the Committee of the House, to whom the former Petition was referred, and within those Limits to which, they are still of Opinion, it would be proper to extend it, in order that the Public may derive the full Benefit of such an Establishment, the Petitioners have again with Regret to state, that, (under the heavy Pressure of Debt, of which an Account is before the House) without further Aid from Parliament, it will be importable to bring to Perfection an Establishment, which, from the Advantages accruing from the more Ikilful Care of so important a Branch of public Property, as the Horses of the Army, is become more than ever an Object of National Importance: And therefore praying, That such Relief may be granted, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Inhabitants within the Borough of Petition from Leeds, in the West Riding of the County of York, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That bf^Oauneal' Meal, made from Oats, constitutes a great Part of the Sustenance of the lower Clafies of the Inhabitants, not only of the said Borough, but of all the populous and manufacturing Parts of that Riding, as well as the Dif-trifts North and West of Yorkshire, and of Scotland also, and that such Meal now is, and for some Time past hath been, at so high a Price that the labouring Poor cannot purchase the same in sufficient Quantities for the Support of their Families, and the Distress arising therefrom is excessive; and the Petitioners further represent, that the great Quantity of Oats consumed by Horses, kept merely for Parade or Pleasure, and of Oatmeal consumed by Dogs, kept merely for Pleasure, contribute much to advance the Price or Oatmeal; and that the Petitioners have great Reason to believe, that such Horses and Dogs are, notwithstanding His Majesty's most gracious Proclamation, kept at their usual Allowance, whilst the labouring Poor, in the Districts above mentioned, are sinking under their Daily Labour, through Famine and Want: And therefore praying. That the House will take the same into their Consideration, and that a Law may be passed, restricting, for a limited Time, the Consumption of Oats and Oatmeal by Horses and Dogs, kept merely for Pleasure.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Committee appointed to consider of the present High Price of Provuions.

A Petition of the Overseers of the Poor of the Town-ftiip of Whitehaven, in Cumberland, was presented to the

House, and read; Setting forth, That the Township of Whitehaven comprehends the Whole of the populous Town of Whitehaven, containing about 15,000 Inhabitants, and about 5,000 Objects liable to be taxed for the Relief of the Poor; and that the making of a perfect Poor Rate in this Township, is wholly impracticable, owing to the vast Number of Persons and Things to be included in the Rate, and the fluctuating State of Property, and of the Occupiers thereof; and that the Petitioners, previous to the last General Quarter Sessions of the Peace for Cumberland, made and published a Rate, which was appealed against by the Right honourable James Earl of Lonsdale, the Lord Lieutenant and Custos Rotulorum of the said County, and, during the Pendency of that Appeal, they were not able to enforce t he Payment of the Rate, whereby the Petitioners were obliged to borrow a large Sum of Money for the Maintenance of the Poor, to prevent their starving in the mean Time; and that, at the said Sessions, this Rate was wholly quashed, because it appeared to the Court that the Names of Two House Owners were therein inserted instead of the Occupiers, although no such Objections were stated in the Notice of Appeal, whereby the Petitioners had no Opportunity of defending themselves against such Objections; and that, as the Law now stands, the Petitioners are advised the Quarter Sessions have Power to quash the whole Rate, for the fmaileft Omission therein, and that it is in i!k;V ower of any Inhabitant to suspend the Collection of the Rate for the whole Space of Time between its Publication and the then following Sections, by appealing against it, inasmuch as the Magistrates cannot safely iliue Distress Warrants thereon, till after such first Sections; and that the Petitioners have published Two other Rates since the last Sections, both of which have been suspended in their Operation, by Appeals brought by the said James Earl of Lonsdale, who, by thus appealing against every Rate the Petitioners make, before they are coileClcd, not only renders such Rates unavailing to the Petitioners for the Relief of the Poor, but induces many of the Persons assessed, to withhold the Payment of the Rates; made good by the Petitioners and other Members of the said Company, so that the Petitioners have paid £.1 7. ioj. for each of their Shares over and above the original Calculation of £.120, which Sums of , and £.17. 10 s.make together/. 13 7. 10 for each

Share, and for the Petitioners Shares the aggregate Sum of ,£.9,587. ior.; and that the said Canal is not completed; and, notwithstanding the above-mentioned Power for railing £. 150,000. for that Purpose, certain Members have devised a Scheme for railing Money for the finishing it, by creating 4,000 new Shares at the reduced Rate of £. 60. for a Share, and to put the Subscribers to such n<*w Shares on an equal Footing with the Petitioners, and the other original Members, who have paid £.137. 10 j. a Share; whereby, in case Vol. 56.

the Income of the said Canal should ever be able to pay j£-5- for a Share, the Subscribers for such new Shares would receive something more than £.8. per Centum on their Subscription, whilst the Petitioners, and other original Members, who have paid such Sum of £.137. 10f. for a Share, would not receive full £.3. 15*. per Centum-, and that the Petitioners conceive such Scheme to be extortionate in the Extreme, as the new Subscribers would run no Rilk, nor fullain much Delay, and, whatever it may be, the Petitioners will sustain the fame; and that the Petitioners admit it to be definable to have the Canal finished, and would not give it unnecessary Delay, but they hope that a Delay of a Year would bring them the Blessing of Peace, and that the necessary Sums for finishing the Canal might then be borrowed at legal Interest; and that the Petitioners have been credibly informed, and believe, that the proposed new Shares are already become an Object of Traffic, and carry a Premium; and that the Petitioners conceive that no Meeting of the Members of the Company is authorized by the said Act of the 34th of His present Majesty, or any other Act, to affix the Seal of ti e Company to any Petition to the House for the Purpose of railing a further Sum of Money, and that the same can be done only by unanimous Content of the Members of the Company; That, in the 2d Year of the lleign of His present Majesty, the said Trustees represented to Parliament, that the Sum allowed them for the Establishment and Support of the said Museum was reduced to a Capital of £.30,000, Reduced Bank Annuities, the Dividend of which, amounting to £. 900, was, notwithstanding their utmost Attention to the forming their Establishment with Frugality, greatly insufficient for that Purpose; upon which Representation they have, at sundry Times, obtained from the House various Sums to supply the Deficiency of their Income; which Sums, together with the Salary allotted to the King's Librarian, Yearly amounting to about 250, have proved insufficient to defray the necessary Expences of the said Museum, and what now remains in the Hands of the Trustees is not sufficient to carry on the Purposes of the Trull without the Aid of Parliament: And therefore praying the House to grant them such farther Support, towards enabling them to carry on the Execution of the Trull reposed in them by Parliament, for the general Benefit of Learning and ul'eful Knowledge, as to the House shall leem meet.

A Petition of Matthew Waddel, of Morpeth, in the County of Northumberland, Cotton Manufacturer, being

offered to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth. That, in the manufacturing of Cotton 'into Mullins, it hath hitherto been nccellary to make use of a Competition called Size, prepared from the fin' ft Wheaten Flour cnly, by which the Consumption of Wheat is very much increased, and its Value proportionably enhanced; and that, in consequence of the Scarcity in the Year 1795, and of the subsequent and present High Price of that great Article of Food, the Petitioner conceived that a Substitute for Flour might be found out in making such Size, to the great Benefit of himlelf, and of ail other the Inhabitants of this King* Voe. 56.

dom; and that, having attentively considered the Advantages to be derived from the Use of such a Substitute, hchath, after repeated and fuccel'sfulTrials, established, in a Cotton ManufaClory at a Substitute for

Wheaten Flour in the making of Size, for the Purpose of fizing and dressing Cotton Webs; and that the Petitioner, on receiving such a Recompence as to the House may fecin equitable, in Consideration of the Benefits already allured to him, and hereafter probably to be derived to the Community, from his Invention, would prefer the Disclosurc of the Secret of preparing this Substitute for Flour, to the obtaining a Patent for it, which would secure all its Emoluments exclusively to himself: And therefore praying the House to take the Subject of his Petition into Consideration, and to make such Order re (peeling it, as by the House may be deemed most meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. HuJkiJJ'on, Mr. Burden, he.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to fend for Persons, Papers, and Records.

stony Strat- Sir William Dolben reported from the Committee, to &<?dPetition wh°m the Petition of the several Persons, whose Names reported. ' are thereunto subscribed, being Trustees in whom certain Charity Estates are now veiled, for the Purpose of repairing the Highways and the Bridge over the River Ouse, in or near the Town of Stony Stratford, in the County of Buckingham, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that no Notices had been given of the Application for paving, cleansing, lighting, and otherwise improving, the Streets, Lanes, and public Passages, and for repairing the Bridge over the River Ouse, in or near the said Town of Stony Stratford, it not having been determined to apply to Parliament in the present Session until the Month of November last, when a Complaint was made by the Postmaster General of the bad State of the Road through the said Town, and Information given, that an Indictment would be presented, if the same was not immediately repaired; but the Committee found that the Expences of 1'uch Repairs and Improvements are proposed to be defrayed by the Sale of certain Estates belonging to the Petitioners, the Annual Rents of which are now applicable for those Purposes; and that it is not proposed to lay any Toll, or to raile any Money by Rates or Assessments upon the Inhabitants of the said Town, or to take down any Houses or Buildings, or entrench upon any private Property, for effecting the Improvements before-mentioned; and that the Committee had also examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth;

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. Richard Allen being examined, said. That the Streets, Lanes, and other public Passages and Places, within the Parishes of Saint Giles and Saint Mary Magdalen, in Stony Stratford, in the County of Buckingham, are not properly paved, cleansed, watered, or lighted, and are subject to various Incroachments, Obllrudions, Nuisances, and Annoyances; and that the Bridge over the River Ouse is very much out of Repair, and otherwise unsafe and incommodious: That the public Highway leading from London to West Chester, passing through the principal Street of the said Town, is become so very much out ot Repair, as to make travelling dangerous, and impede the public Conveyance, in consequence whereof many Persons accustomed to travel through, or resort to, the said Town, have lately omitted

so to do, to the £reat Injury of the Inhabitants j and that His Majesty's Postmaster General had directed an Application to be made to the Clerk of the Trustees for the Reparation of such Road, and Hating, that if the same was not immediately done, their Lord ships Would cause the same to be indicted.- — And the Witness added. That the Assessments made for the Relief of the Poor of the said Parishes are grievously heavy, amounting, upon a fair Average of the last Seven Years, to Twelve Shillings in the Pound upon the Annual Rents of all Property rateable thereto; and that during the last Year, in the Parish of Giles, to the Sum of Thirteen Shillings in the Pound, and in the Parish of Saint Mary Magdalen, to the Sum of Fifteen Shillings in the Pound upon such Rents: That there is great Reason to believe, from the advanced Price of all the Necefiaries of Life, that such Assessments will be much increased during the present Year; in consequence whereof, and of the other public and Parochial Taxes already payable by the Inhabitants of the said Town* the necessary Funds for putting the said Bridge, Streets, Lanes, and ocher public Pallages, into a State of proper Repair, cannot be raised by a Contribution from them, without occasioning very great Distress, or total Ruin, to a great Number of Families. — And the Witness being further examined, said, That divers Messuages, Lands, and Real Estates, have, at different Times, been given to Trustees, and are now vested in the Petitioners, for the Purpose of maintaining and repairing the said Bridge, Streets, and other public Past l'ages and Places; and that the Annual Rents and Profits of the said Trull Estates are by no means sufficient to answer the Purposes aforesaid; but that if the same were fold, and the Monies arising from such Sale applied to defray the Expence of paving, cleansing, lighting, and otherwise improving, the said Streets and other public Passages and Places, and of repairing the said Bridge, it would be of great Benefit to the Inhabitants of the said Town, and all other Persons referring thereto.

Ordered, That the said Report do He upon the Table.
