To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, for the better Relief and Employment of the Poor within the Hundreds of Mitford and in the County of Norfolk, was read: And,

The Reverend Dixon Hoste, being examined, said.

That, under and by virtue of the Powers given by the said Act, the said Hundreds were incorporated, and Directors and Guardians were appointed and chosen, for the Purpose of carrying the Provisions of the said Act into Execution; that Part of a large House was erected for the Reception of the Poor of the said incorporated Hundreds, and a considerable Debt was incurred in building and furnishing the fame; that in pursuance of the Directions of the said Act, a certain fixed Annual Payment or Contribution was charged upon each of the Parishes within the said Hundreds, for the Purpose of defraying the Expences incurred in erecting the said House, and for the Support and Employment of the Poor maintained therein; that the said Act has, under the Experience of upwards of Twenty Years, been found very inadequate to its profefied Object, the better Relief and Employment of the Poor: That the Average Annual Payments, imposed and fixed by the said Act upon the said Parishes, are in many Instancesy and in a high Degree, disproportionate to the manifest Injury of several of the said Parishes: That in Addition to the Mortey originally borrowed, a further Debt, to a considerable Amount, has been unavoidably incurred in the Support and Maintenance of the Poor of the said incorporated Hundreds; and that the Annual Contributions imposed under the said Act, are inadequate to the Purpose of keeping down the Interest of the Debt, and defraying the ordinary Expences of the House, and of supplying the Poor with temporary Relief out of the House: That the said incorporated Hundreds comprize Fifty Parishes, many of which are large and populous, and that from various Errors and Defects in the present System of Management established by the said Act, the Situation of the Poor maintained in the said House is in many Relpefts improper, and that the Children brought up therein become of little or no use to the Community; and the Condition of the labouring Poor residing in the said Hundreds, and endeavouring to maintain themselves and Families by their Labour, is rendered in many Respects miserable and wretched, no Discrimination being made between the worthy and industrious, and the idle and profligate, nor any Encouragement held out to Perseverance in Habits of Sobriety and honest Industry. — And the Witness further said, That it is necessary some effectual Measures should be speedily taken to remedy the Inconveniences and Mischiefs already prevailing, and to provide for the further and better Relief, Support, and Management of the Poor, within the said incorporated Hundreds; and that for this Purpose, it is expedient that certain Parts of the said Act should be repealed, and other Regulations substituted.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to alter, amend, and render more effectual, an Act, passed in the 15th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for the better Relief and Employment of the Poor, within the Hundreds of Milford " and Launditch, in the County of Norfolk:1' And that Sir Martin Browne Folkes, Mr. Coke of Norfolk, and Mr,

AJlley, do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

A Member present informed Your Committee, That the Funds arising from the Duties authorized to be collected by the said Act, have proved insufficient for the Purposes thereby intended, insomuch that the Debt due to the Petitioners has been gradually increasing for many Years, and is likely to continue so to do, Unless the said Funds be increased, by adding to the said Harbour Duties; that notwithstanding the Improvements which have been made under the Authority of the said A«ft, there is (till a very great want of Accommodation for the Ships and Vessels referring to the said Harbour, owing to the small Extent of Docks, and likewise great Inconvenience has arisen to the Merchants and Ship Owners for want of Warehouses, which render additional Works absolutely necessary for the Trade of the said City and Town; that these Accommodations and Conveniences cannot be obtained without great additional Expence, which the Petitioners are willing to defray, on Condition of their being authorized to borrow a further Sum of Money upon the Credit of the said Duties: And it will be necessary, for the Accommodation of the Trade, that Cranes and Sheds should be erected for discharging, loading, covering, and weighing, the Goods imported into, and exported from, the said Harbour; and that certain Cranage and Shed Dues.

That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Turnpike Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr.

Edmund Haworth being examined, said* That the Road leading from The Lamb Inn, otherwise Fletcher's Public House, in Sharpies aforesaid (at which Place it terminates in the Road from Bolton aforesaid to in the said County, being about One Mile from the former Place) to or near Brindle Lane End, otherwise Stoole Lane End, in Hoghton aforesaid (where it forms a Junction with the Road from Blackburn aforesaid, to Preston, in the said County) being 14 computed Miles, and upwards, is very circuitous and indirect, by Reason of the many Windings and Turnings therein, and also is in very bad Repair: That there is not any other eligible Road from the Town of Bolton or Sharpies aforesaid, to Brindle Lane End aforesaid, without going Three Miles about; in which Road there are several steep Hills, feme of which rife Seven Inches at a Yard, and the said Road is in many Places lb narrow, bad, and founderous, that Carts and Carriages cannot pass without much Difficulty; and that the same Road is capable of being diverted in a much more direct Line, and Ihortened, so that the same will not be more than Ten Miles and Three Quarters betwixt the said Place in Sharpies aforesaid, called The Lamb , or Fletcher's Public House, and Brindle Lane End, in Hoghton aforesaid, and will be Three Miles nearer that Way, from the Town of Bolton aforesaid to Preston aforesaid, than the present old Road; and likewise, the said intended new Road will be of very great Advantage and Utility to the Country through which it paifes, the greatest Part thereof being barren and uncultivated, and very much in Want of a good Road.

— That the said Road may also be made so that the greatest Part will not rife more than One Inch at a Yard, other Parts not more than One Inch and a Half, and others not more than Two Inches and a Half, and that only a very short Length of the last- ' mentioned Rife, which will be much more level and easy than the present old Roads from the said Place in Sharpies to Brindle Lane End aforesaid, and also than the present old Road from Bolton to Preston aforesaid, as well as being considerably shorter, as before-mentioned; but the same cannot be effectually diverted, made, repaired, amended, and kept in Repair, by the Laws now in being, to the Danger and Loss of Time of Passengers, and to the Prejudice of Trade and Agriculture in general, and especially of the Cotton Manufactures carried on in the said Towns. —

And the Witness being further examined, said, That the said Manufactures, and also Agriculture, would be greatly increased, extended, and encouraged, if the said Road was diverted, made, amended, and repaired.

Sir James Pulteney reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the several Persons, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, being Owners of Houses, or Ilefidents, within the Parish of Bathwick, near the City of Bath, in the County of Somerset, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Paving Bills, had been complied with; except that the last of the Notices was not published in the Newspapers till the ad of October; and that the Committee had examined

the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Vo l. 56.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. John Salmon being examined, said. That the several Streets, Lanes, Ways, Passages, and Places, within the said Parish, are very . insufficiently paved, fteaned, pitched, cleansed, lighted, and watched, and, for want of a proper and efficient Police, ar$ subject to many Nuisances, Annoyances, Incroachments, and Inconveniencies; that it would tend greatly to the Safety and Accommodation of Persons residing in, or reflirting to, the said Parish, if proper Powers were established for paving, (leaning,pitching, cleansing, lighting, watcli-.ing, and regulating the fame, for removing and preventing Nuisances, Annoyances, and Inconveniencies, and for establishing a proper and efficient Police therein; and also to licence and regulate a convenient Number of Hackney Coaches and Chairs, to limit their Dif-tances, and fix their Fares, with Rules and Orders for their due Regulation. — And the Witnesss further said. That, in order to provide a Fund towards defraying the Expences of carrying into Execution the several Purposes aforesaid, it is expedient that a Toll should be laid on Carriages and Horses conveying Coal through the said Palish; and that a Penalty be on Persons for bathing naked in the River or Canal, within the said Parish.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Corry took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair*

Mr. Corry reported from the Committee, That they had come to several Resolutions; which they had directed him to report, when the Hotile will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be now received.

Mr. Corry accordingly reported from the said Committee, the Resolutions which they had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table; Where the same were read; and are as followeth;

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient, for the more general and speedy Promulgation of the Laws of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, that His Majesty's Printer should be authorized and directed to print not less than 5,500 Copies of every Public General Statute* and 306 Copies of every Public Local and Personal Statute.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee* That His Majesty's Printer should be authorized and directed to print and deliver (or transmit by the Post, or otherwise) so soon as possible after each Bill has received the Royal Assent, the aforesaid Number of 5,500 Copies of each Public General Statute, according to a certain Mode of Distribution.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That His Majesty's Printer should be authorized and directed to print, and deliver or transmit in like Manner, the aforesaid 306 Copies of each Public Local and Personal Statute, according to a certain Mode of Distribution.

Resolved, That'it is the Opinion of this Committee, That every Chief Magistrate and Head Officer of any City, Borough, or Town Corporate, in England and Ireland, and of every Royal Burgh in Scotland, and every

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee* That, for the Purpose of effectuating the Promulgation of Private Statutes (if the Parties interested therein shall think proper) and also for making Compensation to the Clerk of the Parliaments, and Officers of the House of Lords (in lieu of their Annual Average Emoluments arising from the Office Copies of such Statutes) without bringing any new Charge upon the Public, the Parties interested in every such Statute should make good such Expence and Compensation; and that thereupon such printed Copies of every such Statute should be made judicially admissible in Evidence, by adding thereto a Clause declaring the same to be a Public Act.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That His Majesty's Printer should also be authorized and directed to class the General Statutes, and the Public Local and Personal Statutes of each Session, in separate Volumes, and to number the Chapters of each Class separately; and also, to print One General Title to each Volume, together with a General Table of all the Acts passed in that Session.

Winchester Sir Rickard Gamon reported from the Committee, to SlTlPe~ whom the Petition of the Mayor, Bailiffs, and Comported! monafty, of the City of in the County of Southampton; and also, another Petition of the Mayor, Bailiffs, and Commonalty, of the City of were federally referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petitions, and had directed him to- report the fame, as they appeared to them, to the House-; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth j viz.

To prove the Allegations of the first-mentioned Petition, John Ridding, Esquire, being examined, said. That the Gaol or Bridewell belonging to the said City, has for many Years been much out of Repair, and large Sums of Money have, at different Times, been expended in and about the Repairs of the fame, until at length the same became so ruinous, that the Petitioners, after haring examined skilful Workmen respecting the State of the fame, found that it could not be repaired, so that it might any longer be used with Safety as a Place of Confinement for Persons committing Offences within the Jurisdiction of the said City, without incurring an Expence nearly equal to the Expence of taking down and re-building the same; it was therefore judged expedient wholly to take down the fame, in order that the Materials thereof might be used in erecting and building another Gaol or Bridewell in its Head: That the Expences of taking down and re-building of which, exclusive of the old Materials which have been made use of, will amount to a considerable Sum of Money, and much more than the Petitioners are able to discharge, without the Alii fiance of Parliament, to enable them to xaife a competent Sum of Money for that Purpose, by One or more Rate or Rates upon the Owners and Occupiers of Messuages, Lands, or Tenements, within the said City. — Then,

To prove the Allegations of the second-mentioned Petition, Mr. Ridding being further examined, said. That there are Six old Houses or Tenements, situate close to the said Gaol or Bridewell, by the removing and taking down of which, not only much Advantage will be derived to the said new Gaol, but great Convenience will result to the Public by widening the Street, which in its present State is much too narrow: That for this Reason, it having been judged adviseable to remove the said Houses or Tenements, a Meeting of the Inhabitants of the said City has been convened, in consequence of a Requisition made to the Petitioners by the said Inhabitants to take the Measure, into Consideration, when it was unanimously refoived, that the fame, if it could be carried into Effedt, would be of great public Benefit.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That the Trade between this Kingdom and Turkey has, for a long Series of Years, been carried on by a Society of Merchants^incorporated by Charters, and regulated by Acts of Parliament; and that, in order to carry on this Trade with Safety, and protect His Majesty's Subjects in the Turkish Dominions, it has been found necessary, that an Ambassador, or Public Minister, should be sent from England to reside at j

and that Consuls, Vice Consuls, with proper Officers, and Servants, should be -established in other Parts of

Turkey, where British Subjects reside, and where the

English Merchants carry on Trade, the whole Expence of which has been borne by the Company, which, together with other Expences incident to carrying on this Trade, have, of late Years, amounted to about

8,000. per Annum; and that the Petitioners feel it incumbent on them to represent, that the House, which has always been appropriated for the Reception of His Majesty's Ambassadors at The Porte, is fallen to Decay, ?nd it will be necessary to cause a new one to be built, in case it should be thought expedient to provide a permanent Residence for a Public Officer of so much Consequence; a Measur which muff be left to the Wisdom of Parliament, and, if adopted, will necessarily be attended with considerable Expence; and that the Petitioners acknowledge, with Gratitude, the Grants they have frequently received; but they are sensible they should not discharge the Duty incumbent on them by their Charter, nor the Justice which they owe to the Public (for whom they consider themselves asTrustees), if they did not declare their present Inability to defray so heavy a Charge, and to support their Establishments in

Turkey, without the Assistance of Parliament: And therefore praying the House to take these Premises into Consideration, and grant them such Relief as may be thought necessary and proper.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Resolved, That this House will, at the Riling of the House this Day, adjourn till Monday Morning next.

Mr. Abbot reported from the Select Committee, who keport re-were appointed to consider of so much of the Fourth [dd by irioT Article of the Union between Great Britain and Ireland, Member*, as enacts. That no greater Number of Members than Twenty, holding Offices or Places of Profit under the Crown of Ireland, shall be capable of fitting in the House of Commons of the Parliament of the United Kingdom, until an Act shall have passed in the said Parliament, providing in what Cafes Persons holding such Offices or Places shall be incapable of being Members of the said House of Commons; and to consider in what Cafes Persons holding such Offices or Places shall be declared to be liable to such Incapacity; and to report their Opinion thereupon to the House; That the Committee had considered the Matters to them re*-ferred, and had directed him to make a Report thereof, together with several Resolutions of the Committee thereupon, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth) viz.

Your Committee having proceeded to consider the several Matters to them referred, have thought it incumbent upon them, in the First Place, to look into the several Laws, whereby Persons have been heretofore disqualified from fitting in the House of Commons of the respective Parliaments of Great Britain and Ireland.

Upon this Research, it has appeared to Your Committee, That several Laws of this Nature were enacted, for securing the Freedom and Independence of the House of Commons of England antecedently to the Union with Scotland-, and that many Acts for the same Purposes have been passed in the Parliament of Great Britain from that Period. In Ireland, the First Laws of this Nature were passed in the Reign of His present Majesty; the most comprehensive of them was enacted within a very few Years past, and has been since extended to other Cafes, which, although not falling within the express Terms of it, were considered to be within the same Rule of Policy; but the Laws respecting the Parliament of Ireland, are manifestly much more circumscribed in their Operation than those which have been made, for the same Purposes, as applicable to the Parliament of Great Britain.

With a View therefore to fulfil the particular Duty required of Y our Committee, and to lay the Foundation for a new Law, declaring in what Cafes any Persons holding Offices of Profit, under the Crown of Ireland, shall be incapable of fitting in the House of Commons of the United Parliament, it has appeared to Your Committee, that it would be adviseable to establish a Similarity of System upon this Subject, in both Parts of the United Kingdom, so far as Circum-llances will allow; and that all Offices in Ireland, of the same Description as those which have disqualified the Persons who held them from being elected to' serve as

Members

384 8° Mail*1801.

Members of the House of Corftmons of Great Britain, should also disable any Persons, who hold them, from being elected to serve in the United Parliament. And Your Committee have accordingly prepared a List of all such Offices, as have appeared to them to be of that Description; submitting, nevertheless, to the Wisdom of the House, the Propriety of adding to, or excepting the reout, any such Offices, as, from peculiar Circumstances of Policy ( or local Convenience, it may be thought beneficial for the Public Service to consider as fit Cafes for departing from that Principle of Conformity, which Your Committee have judged to be the best general Line for the Government of their own Opinion upon this Subject.

Your Committee have therefore come to the following Resolutions; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, from and after the Difiblution, or other Determination of this present Parliament, no Person who shall, by himself or his Deputy, or any other in Trust for him, or for his Benefit, take, hold, enjoy, or execute, or continue to hold, enjoy, or execute any of the Offices, Employments, or Places of Profit herein after mentioned, in or for that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, should be capable of being elected or chosen a Member of, or of fitting or voting as a Member of the House of Commons of any Parliament of the said United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, in any Parliament which shall hereafter be summoned and holden; that is to say;

No Person who shall be a Commissioner of Customs, Excise, or Stamps, or who shall be concerned directly or indirectly in the farming, collecting, or managing any of the Sums of Money, Duties, or other Aids heretofore granted, or which shall hereafter be granted by any Act of Parliament to His Majesty, His Heirs, or Successors; (except the Commissioners of the Treasury and their Secretary);

Nor any Person who shall be a Commissioner for determining Appeals concerning the said Duties of Customs, Excise, and Stamps, or for controuling or auditing the Account of the said Duties; (except the Auditor General of the Exchequer);

Nor any Person who shall be a Commissioner of Im-prest Accounts j

Nor any Agent for any Regiment;

Nor any Person who shall, directly or indirectly, himself, or by any Person whatsoever in Trust for him, or for his Use or Benefit, or on his Account, undertake, execute, hold, or enjoy, or continue to execute, hold, or enjoy, in the Whole or in Part, any Contraft, Agreement, or Commission, made or entered into, under or from the Commissioners of His Majesty's Trea-fuTy in Ireland, or with any One or more of such Commissioners, or with any other Person or Persons whatsoever, for or on Account of the Public Service in Ireland, or who shall knowingly and willingly furnish or provide, in pursuance of any such Agreement, Contraft, or Commission, which he or they shall have made or entered into as aforesaid, any Money to be remitted Abroad, or any Wares or Merchandize to be used or employed in the Service of the Public, during the Time that he shall execute, hold, or enjoy any such Contract, Agreement, or Commission, or any Part or Share thereof, or any Benefit or Emolument arising from the same j (except Persons who shall be Members of any incorporated Trading Company now existing or established in Ireland, and confiding of more than Ten Persons, so far as relates to any Contraft, Agreement, or Commission, which now is, or shall or may hereafter be made, entered into, or accepted, by such Company, in its Corporate Capacity, for the general Benefit of such Incorporation or Company);

Nor any Deputies or Clerks in any of the several Offices following j that is to say j the Office of Lord High Treasurer, or the Commissioners of the Treasury; (except the Secretary of the Treasury); or of the Auditor of the Receipt of His Majesty's Exchequer, or of the Tellers of the Exchequer, or of the Chancellor of the Exchequer; (except the Secretary of the Chancellor of Exchequer); or of the Commissioners of the Stamps, or of the Commissioners of Appeals;

Nor any Person who shall have in his own Name, or in the Name of any Person or Persons in Trust for him, or his Benefit, any Office or Place of Profit, either immediately or directly under the Crown, or from or by the Nomination or Appointment, or by any other Appointment, subject to the Approbation of the Lord Lieutenant, Lord Deputy, Lord Justices, or other Chief Governor or Governors of that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, created or eroded at any Time after the passing of an Act of the Parliament of Ireland in the 33d Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for securing the " Freedom and Independence of the House of Commons, by excluding therefrom Persons holding any " Offices under the Crown to be hereafter created, or " holding certain Offices therein enumerated, or Penfions for Terms or Years, or during His Majesty's " Pleasure."

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That nothing in the preceding Resolution should extend, or be construed to extend, or relate to, or exclude any Person having or holding any Office, Place, or Employment for Life, or for so long as he shall behave himself well in his Office, other than and except all Persons concerned in the managing, collecting, or farming of the said Duties, or of any Sums of Money, Duties, or other Aids granted, or to be granted to His Majesty, His Heirs, or Successors, and Commissioners for auditing the Public Accounts.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That such a Number of Copies of the said Report be printed, as shall be sufficient for the Use of the Members of the House.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mn Nathaniel Clayton being examined, said, That the Petitioners baVe been for a long Series of Years a Corporation, and have exercised and enjoyed various Powers and Privileges, and particularly the Power of appointing and licensing Pilots for conducting Ships or Vessels, and of erecting, placing) and maintaining Lights, Buoys, and Beacons, in the Port of Newtajlle and River Tyne, and have received and taken divers Rates and Duties in respect of the Charges and Expences attending the Exercise and Performance of such Powers and Privileges, whereby the Trade and Navigation of the said Port and River, and of the Creeks and Members thereof, have been much promoted and increased; but that the Powers of Control over the said Pilots arc insufficient for their effectual Government, and that the Rates and Duties have become inadequate to the increased Expence attending the Ufc and Exercise of the said Powers and Privileges, by means whereof the Petitioners are restrained in the full Use and Exercise of such their Privileges, to the Prejudice of the increasing Trade of the said Port and River. — And the Witness further said, That a Doubt has arisen, whether the Creek or Haven of Holy Island, lying off the Coast of the County of

Northumberland, is a Creek or Member belonging to the said Port of Newcastle, although the Petitioners, at the

Request of the Owners of Ships and Vessels using the Coasting Trade on the East Side of Great Britain, have lately, at a great Expence, erected Beacons there, which have already conduced greatly to the Security of such Ships and Vessels; and it will be further beneficial if such Creek or Haven was declared to be a Creek belonging to the said Port of Newcastle, in so far as to enable the Petitioners to support and maintain Buoys and Beacons, and to appoint and license Pilots for the piloting and conducting Ships and Vessels into, and out of, the said Creek or Haven of Holy Island; and that it will further conduce to the Security and Convenience of Ships and other Vessels retorting to the Port of Newcastle, if the Conservators of the River Tyne were enabled to appoint a Harbour Matter, or Harbour Matters, for the said Port and River, with the necessary Powers incident to the Office of Harbour Matter.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for extending and enlarging the Powers, and increasing the Rates and Duties of the Corporation of the Trinity House of Newcastle upon Tyne, and for better regulating the Port of Newcastle: And that Sir Matthew White Ridley, Mr. Grey, Mr. Burdon, and Mr. Brandling, do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

Sir William Geary reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Landholders, Hop Planters, and others, interested in the Cultivation of Hops in the Counties of Kent and Suffix, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. William Randall being examined, said, That Hops, from the Extent of their Cultivation in the Counties of Kent and Sussex, may be considered as forming the Staple

Commodity of those Counties: That, independent of the Advantage derived to the Revenue, Hops have been admitted to be the most salutary Ingredient in the Bit-tering and Preservation of that useful Beverage, Beer: That the System hitherto adopted, of felling Hops in the private Houses of Factors, has tended to the En-

Maii. A. 1801.

couragement of Monopoly, and, consequently, to the great Injury and Inconvenience of the Public at large j and the Want of a public Market in or near the Metropolis, has long been universally acknowledged: That the Establishment of such Market would, at the same Time that it accelerated the Sale of this Product, the most expensive in its Cultivation of any other Species of Agriculture, essentially promote the Advantage of the Public, by affording a fair and general Competition.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to enable certain Persons to erect a Market for the Sale of Hops, in the Borough of Southwark, in the County of Surrey: And that Sir William Geary and Sir Edward Knatchbull, do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

That the said Forest, or Chace, is stated by the said Bill to contain 9,400 Acres, and that there are Twenty-two Parishes, Townships, Hamlets, and Districts, surrounding, or near to, the said Forest, or Chace; and the Owners or Occupiers thereof have Right of Common thereon (that is to say) the Owners or Occupiers of 700 Mefiiiages, or thereabouts, have Right of Common, for each Messuage,

and the Lords and Ladies of the said Manor have Common Right thereon; and many Copyhold Estates are held of the said Manors, which have Right of Common on the said Forest, or Chace; but no sufficient or suitable Provision is made itt the said Bill for Allotments of Land in lieu of such Rights, nor for the preserving the Rights of the Lords and Copyholders thereon; and that, from the Form and Amount of the Compensations proposed by the said Bill to be made to His Majesty, in Lieu of His Rights and Interest in, and over the said Forest, the Petitioners conceive those Rights to be misunderstood, or greatly over-rated; and that His Majesty, in Right of the said Duchy, claims the Timber and Underwood as His exclusive Property, which Claim the Petitioners conceive to be not well founded; and that His Majesty, as the Petitioners apprehend, has no Right of Common on the said Forest, or Chace, for Horses, Cows, or other Cattle, except for the Four Lodges within the Four Wards of the Forest; and there are no Sheep fed, or allowed to be depastured or kept thereon; and the Cows, Horses, and other Beasts, actually kept and fed by the Petitioners and the other Commoners, or which they have a Right to keep on the said Forest, or Chace, together with the Deer, are more than lulficient to consume the Whole Herbage thereof; nevertheless, by the said Bill, as it is at present framed, one Moiety only of the said Forest, or Chace, is allotted to the Freeholders and Persons havingRight of Common, and the Residue thereof is supposed to be allotted to His Majesty (subject to an Allotment in Lieu of Tythes, and some other small Deductions) together with all the large Timber growing thereon, and great Part of the rest of the Wood; and that the Petitioners are advised, that such Allotments of Land as are made to the Owners of Common Rights in the said Parishes, Town-ships, Hamlets, and Districts, ought to be made to each of those Parishes, Townships, Hamlets, or Districts, according to the respective Rights appertaining to each District; and that the Payment for laxes and Parish Rates should be aflelied in each of such Districts to which the same Allotments respectively belong; and that Allotments, in Lieu of Tythes, should be made to the Redtors and Vicars of such Parishes and Districts, and" not to the Four Parishes only which are mentioned in the said Bill; Kempton, thereby directed to be divided, allotted, and inclosed, as should be equal in Value to One-Sixteenth Part of such Waste Lands and Grounds, for the respective Right and Interest of the said Lord of the said Manor, in or to the said Residue of the said Waste Lands and Grounds, or to the Soil thereof (exclusive of any separate or distinct Right which the said Lord might have in or to the Soil of the said Waste Lands and Grounds) within, or of, or belonging to, the said Manor,' and within the respective Parishes of Feltham and Sunbury; and that the said Commissioners have proceeded to carry the said Act into Execution; and that at one of the Meetings of the Commissioners, the Steward or Agent of the said Edmund Hill, and Who had been employed as the Solicitor in procuring the said Act, produced before the Commissioners, in the course of their Enquiries respecting some Rights claimed within the said Manor of Colkenington, otherwise Kempton, a Book, containing the Customs of that Manor, and, upon the Examination of which, the following Entry appeared therein: "Ini 747 a Court of Survey of the Manor of " Cold Kensington, otherwise Kempton, was held, and the " Jury thereupon found as follows; videlicet. That, by " tomeAgreement between ‘SwRobert Knight,

" a former Lord of this Manor, and the Tenants of the " fame, the said Sir Robert did inclose a Parcel of " Kempton Common, from the Corner of a Hedge " called Broomfield Corner, or Pill Corner, on the North, " towards a Gate called Kempton Gate, towards the " South; and that the said Tenants, did relcafe their " Right thereto; and that in Consideration thereof, " the said Tenants were to be at Liberty to inclose the " rest of the said Common to their own Use, at and " under the like Rents, Customs, and Services, as they " enjoy their inclosed Lands within the said Manor; for, had they been made acquainted therewith, they should have oppoled the Allowance so made to the said Lord by the said Act, and should have endeavoured to have procured a Clause to be inserted therein, giving them Power to try their Right in one of His Majesty's Courts of Law in Westminster Hall; and that the Petitioners applied to the said Commissioners, and requested them not to make any Allotment to the said Edmund Hill of the aforesaid One-Sixteenth Part of the Waste Lands and Grounds within the said Manor; I am to acknowledge the Receipt of Your's of the x 6th Instant, inclosing me, by Order of the Honourable House of Commons, their llefolutions approving my Conduct, and that of the Flag Officers, Captains, and Officers, as also that of the Seamen, Marines, and Soldiers, under my Command on the 2d of April, which I have communicated to the Fleet.

My own Feelings are so much affected at this Mark of my Country's Approbation, as to render me unequal to find Words expressive of my Senlibility on the marked Honour; and I have only to request you. Sir, to affine the House, it will serve to re-animate a Life, nearly exhaulted, after Fifty Years l'pent in my Country's Service.

You, Sir, I am to desire will accept my bell Thanks for the very handsome Manner in which you are plealed to express yourlclf; and that you will believe me, with the highest Respect and Esteem,

Your most obedient.

And very humble Servant,

Hyde Parker.

fire His Majesty, That He will be graciously pleased to- Abercromby. give Directions, that a Monument be erected in the Cathedral Church of Saint Pail's, London, to the Memory of the ever-lamented late Commander in Chief of His Majesty's Land Forces, on an Expedition against the French on the Coast of Egypt, Lieutenant General the Right honourable Sir Ralph Abercromby, Knight of the most Honourable Order of the Bath, who, having surmounted, by consummate Ability and Valour, the Obstacles opposed to his Landing by local Difficulties, and a powerful and well-prepared Enemy, and having successfully established and maintained the fuc-ceflive Politions necessary for conducting his further Operations, refilled, with signal Advantage, a desperate Attack of chosen and veteran Troops on the 21st Day of March 1801, when he received, early in the Engagement, a mortal Wound, but remained in the Field, guiding by his Direction, and animating by his Pre-lence, the brave Troops under his Command, till they had achieved the brilliant and important Victory obtained on that memorable Day; and to allure His Majesty, that this House will make good the Expence of erecting the said Monument.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the 31st Year of His present Majesty's Reign, for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from Manchester, to or near Presto-lee* Bridge, in the Township of Little Lever, and from thence by one Branch to or near the Town of Bolton; and by another Branch to or near the Town of Bury, and to Weddell Brooks in the Parish of Bury, all in the County Palatine of Lancester, was read: And,

Mr. John Nightingale being examined, said. That the Petitioners have proceeded to cut the said Canal, pursuant to the Directions of the said Act, and have made great Progress towards the Completion thereof; and, in the Execution of the lame, have expended the several Sums of Money authorized to be raised under the Powers of the said Act; but it will require a further Sum of Money to enable the Petitioners to make navigable and complete the said Canal, and to pay the Debts incurred, and now due and owing: That it is proposed, that some Variation should be made in the Tonnage Rates, and that the said Act should in some other respects be altered and amended.

Mr. Dickinsonreported from the Committee, who were appointed to consider of the Persons to be appointed Commissioners, Surveyors, and Valuers, in Bills of Inclosure and Drainage, and to report the lame, with their Opinion thereupon, to the House; That the Committee had considered the Matter to them referred; and had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Resolutions of the Committee were read; and are as followeth;

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, in every Bill for inclosing any Moors, Commons, Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, and in every Bill for draining any Low Lands, there be inserted a Clause or Clauses to prevent any Lord, or the Steward or Bailiff of any Lord or Lady of any Manor or Manors extending over the Whole, or over any Part of the said Moors, Commons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, intended to be by such Bill inclosed, or Low Lands intended to be by such Bill drained, and also to prevent any Proprietor or Person interested, or the Steward, Bailiff, or Agent, of any Proprietor or Person interested in such Moors, Commons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, intended to be by such Bill inclosed, or Low Lands intended to be by such Bill drained, from acting as Commissioner, Surveyor, or Valuer, for the inclosing such Moors, Commons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, or for the draining such Low Lands.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, in every Bill for the inclosing any Moors, Commons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, or for the draining of any Low Lands, there be inserted an Oath or Oaths, Affirmation or Affirmations, to be taken by every Commissioner, Surveyor, and Valuer, of Lands intended to be by such Bill inclosed or drained, that they are not interested in the

Lands so intended to be inclosed of drained, or is Steward, Bailiff, or Agent, of any Person so interested.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That such a Number of Copies of the said Report be printed, as shall be sufficient for the Use of the Members of the House.

Lord Granville Levejon Gower reported froth the Corti- Report from mittee, who were appointed to consider of giving Powers to Justices of the Peace, for the more effec- considerot tually repairing County Bridges, and to report the fame, with their Opinion thereupon, to the House; Bridge! and to whom the Report which, upon the 30th Day of May 1800, was made from the Committee appointed to consider of giving Power to Justices of the Peace for the more effectually repairing County Bridges, and also Of the Steps proper to be taken previous to the building of Bridges that are to be deemed County Bridges, and of empowering Justices of the Peace, in their Quarter Sessions, to alter the Situation of County Bridges, and to widen and enlarge the fame, and the Roads at the Ends thereof; and likewise to consider of empowering Justices to direct Actions to be brought, in the Name of the Clerk of the Peace, for Damages done to County Bridges, County Gaols, Bridewells, and other County Works, was referred; and who were instrufted to consider of the several Matters referred to in the said Report; That the Committee had considered the Matters to them referred; and had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Resolutions of the Committee were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the Powers given by the different Statutes now in Force, relative to the Repair of County Bridges, are in some Respects defective.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the Surveyors of County Bridges, appointed by Justices of the Peace at their General Quarter Sessions,

should have the same Power to get, take, and carry away Stones, Gravel, Sand, and other Materials, for the Repair of Roads over Bridges, and the Roads for the Space of Three Hundred Feet at each of the Ends thereof, as are given to the Surveyors of Highways by virtue of an Act, passed in the 13th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, making Satisfaction for the Damages done thereby, in the same Manner as is directed by the said Act.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the Justices of the Peace, in General Quarter Sessions, should be empowered to alter the Situation of County Bridges, and to widen and enlarge the fame, and the Roads, for the Space of Three Hundred Feet at each of the Ends thereof, and to order their Surveyor to agree for the Recompence to be made for the Ground to be taken for those Purposes; and, if the said Surveyor cannot agree with the Persons, Bodies Politic or Corporate, who are seised and possess'ed of such Ground, or if they cannot be found, or shall refuse to treat, or take such Recompence as shall be offered to them respectively by such Surveyor, then the said Justices shall have Power to empannel a Jury at the Quarter Sessions, to assess the Damages to be given, and the Recompence to be made to the Owners, and others, interested in the said Grounds, in the Manner directed by the said Act, of the 13th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, in respect of the widening of Highways; and if the Jury shall give a Verdict for more Money than was offered by the said Surveyor, the Costs of the Proceedings to be paid by the said Surveyor; but if the Jury shall give a Verdict for no more, or for less, than was offered by the Surveyor, then the Costs to be paid by the Person, or Body Corporate,

4i Geo. IIL 190

porate, who refused to accept the Satisfaction so offered to him; and that on Payment or Tender of the Money so to be awarded, on leaving it in the Hands of the Clerk of the Peace, if the Party entitled to receive it cannot be found, or shall refuse to accept it, the Interest of such Person shall beditrested out of him j saying nevertheless to the Owner of the Ground all Mines and Minerals which may be got without breaking the Ground, and all Timber and Wood growing on such Ground.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Powers and Provisions of the said Statute, of the 13th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, relative to Highways, and the Surveyors of Highways in general* be extended to County Bridges, and Roads at the Ends thereof, and the Surveyors of such Bridges and Roads, as far as the same can be extended and applied.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Inhabitants of Counties should^have Power of firing, and being sued, in the Name of their Surveyor, or iome other public Officer.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Counties should not be bound to maintain and repair any Bridge hereafter to be built, unless the Afagi ft rates, in General Quarter Sessions assembled, should determine that such Bridge is necessary to be built for the Purposes of the Public, and should consent thereto.

Ordered, That the said Report be taken into further Consideration upon Friday Morning next.

Ordered, That such a Number of Copies of the said Report be printed, as shall be sufficient for the Use of the Members of the House.

and that, with a View to give Relief to the Petitioner and his Family, in Consideration of the Hardship of their Cafe, which had been entirely occasioned by an extraordinary Interposition of the Legislature to their Prejudice, in consequence of the Imposition practised as before stated, an Act was passed in the Year 1794, whereby, after reciting to the Effect aforesaid, and that the said Richard Rig by, the Mortgagee of the aforesaid Estates, died indebted to the Crown in a very large Sum of Money, of which there was then £,140,000, and upwards due; and also reciting, that the Petitioner was delirous of having the said mortgaged Estates veiled in Trust for himself and his Family, upon his procuring to be paid into His Majesty's Exchequer fuel) Sum of Money as, under the aggravated Distrefsofhis Cafe, attended with all its peculiar Circumstances, Parliament, in their Wisdom and Humanity, should think reasonable; and, in order thereto, the Petitioner humbly proposed, that it might be referred to the Lords Commissioners of the Treasury, to inquire into, and ascertain, what Sum was reasonable and proper to be paid into the Exchequer; and Provision is made by the said Act, for efteeftuating the other Purposes mentioned in the Recitals thereof; and that the Whole of the Personal Estate of the said Richard Rigby, except the mortgaged Property in question, has been applied towards Satisfaction of the said Richard Rigby's Debt to the Crown, which is thereby reduced to the Sum of £.90,000, or thereabouts: But inasmuch as the Real Estates of the said Richard Rigby are found to be more than sufficient to discharge the Residue of the said Debt to the Crown, and therefore that it will not be necessary to resort to the said mortgaged Premises to recover the Balance so due, whereby the Petitioner and his Family find themselves deprived of any Relief under the said Act, which he cannot but presume it was the Intention of the Legislature to afford them, notwithstanding the Condition above recited, which he apprehends was introduced by Mistake, as being contrary to the Object of the Petition on which the said Act was founded, and the Principle on which it was favourably received by Parliament: And therefore Praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for explaining and amending the said last mentioned Act in the Particular aforesaid, or for such Relief in the Premises as to the House shall feein meet.

MR. Vyner reported from the Committee, to whom Boston

the Petition of the Mayor, Aldermen, and Com- Bridge, &c mon Council, of the Borough of in the County £^£n're*

of Lincoln, was referred; 'That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Bills for building Bridges, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr.

John Rennie, an Engineer, being examined, said, That the Bridge over the River Witha in the Borough of Boston, in the County of Lincoln, is much too narrow, and at present in a very decayed and ruinous State and Condition, and is become inconvenient and dangerous to Passengers, Carriages, and Cattle passing over the fame; and therefore, it is necessary to take down and re-build the said Bridge, and also to widen, raise, and render more commodious, several Streets, Lanes, or Ways, leading or near thereto, and to purchase and take down several Houses and Buildings for that Purpose. —

And he added, That the Situation of the present Bridge is very inconvenient, and that therefore it will tend greatly to the Improvement of the said Borough, if the intended new Bridge was erected in a more proper and convenient Situation, very near the present Bridge; and in such Case, it will be necessary to purchase and take down several Houses and Buildings. — Then,

Mr. Samuel Tunnard being examined, said. That the Gaol and House of Correction of the said Borough is at present in a very decayed State and Condition, and by lleafon of the confined Situation thereof, and for want of a free Circulation of Air, the said Gaol and House ot Correction is become very unhealthy and dangerous to the Lives of the Persons confined therein; and, that it is become highly necessary that the said Gaol and House of Correction should be enlarged, and a proper and fuitable Prison Yard added thereto; and for that Purpose, it will be necessary to purchase and take down several Houses and Buildings. — And he added. That the Market Cross of the said Borough, and several of the Rooms over the fame, which are appropriated for the Transaction of public Business, within the said Borough, are too final], and at present very inconvenient and incommodious; and it is become necessary that the said Market Cross and Rooms should be enlarged, and made more convenient to Persons resorting thereto, or having Occasion to use the fame.

GEORGE R.

His Majesty, having taken into His Royal Consideration the eminent and signal Merits of the late Right honourable General Sir Ralph Knight of the Most honourable Order of the Bath, during a long Life spent in the Service of his Country, and terminated by a glorious Death, has thought proper, in Testimony of Regard to the Memory of that distinguished Officer, to confer on his Relict, Lady Abercromby, the‘Dignity of a Barony of Great Britain, by the Title of Baronets Abercromby of AbouLir, with Remainder to the Heirs Male of the Body of the said Sir Ralph Abercromby: And being further desirous of granting to Lady and the

Two next tuccceding Heirs Male of the Body of Sir Ralph Abercromby, to whom the Title ot Baron Abercromby thall defeend, a Nett Annuity of Two Thousand Pounds per Annum, recommends it to His faithful Commons to consider of a proper Method of enabling His Majesty to grant such Annuity, and of extending, securing, and settling the fame, in such Manner as Hull be thought 5

most effectual for the Benefit of the Family of the said Sir Ralph Abercromby. G. R.

A Petition of the there-undersigned Persons, being Butchers; residing within the Borough of Tezvkesbury, in the County of Gloucester, and in several Parishes and Hamlets contiguous thereto, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of an Act, passed in the last Session of Parliament, to repeal so much of an Act, passed in the 2d Year of the Reign of King James the First, as prohibits the Use of Horse Hides in making Boots and Shoes, and for better preventing the damaging of Raw Hides and Skins in the Flaying thereof; and containing Allegations to the same Effect as the Petitions which have been before presented to the House relating the reto: And praying the House to take their same into Consideration; and that Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for repealing the said Act.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Tanners, Curriers, Shoemakers, Sadlers, Coachmakers, and other Artificers, concerned in the cutting and using of Leather, in the City of Coventry, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That an Act was obtained in the 39th and 40th Years of His present Majesty's Reign, for the better preventing the damaging of Raw Hides and Skins in the Flaying thereof, which has been found very beneficial to the Leather Trade, and of considerable Advantage to the Public in general: And praying, That the said Act may not be repealed.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the several Persons whose Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf, of themselves and others, engaged in the Ribbon Manufactory in the City of Coventry, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the Bill for the better Relief and Employment of the Poor in the several Parishes of Saint Michael and The Holy Trinity, in the City of Coventry, and County of the same City; and Setting forth, That, if the same should pass into a Law, it will be injurious to the Petitioners, and to all Persons concerned or employed in the said Ribbon Manufactory, inasmuch as the Directors, intended to be appointed by the said Bill, will be enabled to establish a public Ribbon Manufactory, and the Goods, when so manufactured, will have it in their Power to fell at a much lower Price than the Petitioners, who are engaged in carrying on the said Manufactory, can afford to do, which will greatly injure the Petitioners, and their Families; and that, in the House of Industry established at the Town of Bedworth, near the

Guardians or Directors employ the Poor in manufacturing Ribbons, which Ribbons they actually fell at a Price much lower than the fair and usual manufacturing Price, which has already greatly injured the Petitioners, and prevented them from being employed, as they otherwise would have been; and they are leriously alarmed, that the Directors to be appointed by the said Bill, unless restrained therefrom, will manufacture Ribbons in the said House of Industry intended to be established, under the Provisions contained therein: And

therefore praying, That the said Bill may not pass into a Law.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

To

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the Year 1794, intituled, "An Act to " enable the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty's " Treasury, to ascertain what Sum shall be paid into " His Majesty's Exchequer, in full Satisfaction of the Debt due on the Mortgage made by the late John " Gardner Kemeys, Esquire, in Trust for the late Right

honourable Richard Rigby, in case it shall appear to " the said Lords Commissioners, that it will be necessary to resort to the mortgaged Premises, in order <c to recover the Balance due from the said Richard Rigby to His Majesty," was read; whereby it appeared, that in the Year 1756, John Gardner Kemeys, El quire, the Petitioner's Father, intermarried with Mils Jane Kemeys, whereupon the Estates of the said John Gardner Kemeys, in the Island of Jamaica, then of the Annual Value of £.1,200, or thereabouts, and also, the Estates of Miss Jane Kemeys, in the County of Monmouth, of the Yearly Value of £.35o, or thereabouts, were settled, after the Death of the said John Gardner Kemeys, in strict Settlement upon the Issue Male of such Marriage, subject to the then Incumbrances of £-3,300, and also subject to a Jointure of £. 500 per Annum to Miss Kemeys, and the Sum of £. 4,000, as a Provision for the Younger Children of such Marriage; and it also appeared, that in the Year 1772, the Petitioner's said Father having involved himself in Debt, as well for Money borrowed at Interest, as also taken up for Annuities granted by. him to the Amount, as calculated, of£.44,026, applied to Parliament to open the Settlement, and to make a Security for that Sum, in Preference to the Settlement, on a Pretence, utterly unfounded, that a great Part of his Debts had been incurred for the Sums he had advanced to add new Estates to, and improve the settled Estates; and it further appeared, that in consequence of the greatest Imposition on, and the moll false Representations to the Legislature, an Act was passed in the said Year 1772, when the Petitioner was an Infant of about Fourteen Years of Age, to open the Settlement, and to charge the Estates, both settled and unsettled, with the Sum of £.44,026, and the growing Interest of the Debts and Arrears of the Annuities, in Preference to the Settlement; and in that Year 1772, the late Right honourable Richard Rigby advanced the Sum of £.48,000 on a Mortgage made by the Trustees of the Act; but it appearing that the Trustees had exceeded their Power, the Principal of the said Mortgage was afterwards reduced by a Decree of the Court of Chancery to £. 41,386. 13; and it further appeared, that in July 1793, the Petitioner's said Father died insolvent, leaving the said Jane Gardner Kemeys, his Widow, and the Petitioner, his only Son, and Jane Gardner Kemeys, now the Wife of Providence Hansard, Esquire, and Snfanna Margaret Gardner ,*

his only Daughter him surviving; and upon that Event, the Petitioner, upon looking into his Affairs, found himself absolutely ruined, his Estate taken from him, and not only himself, but also his Mothc.- and his Two Sifters, left entirely destitute of any Provision, they having no other Fortune but what was intended for them by the above Settlement; and it being supposed that the said Richard Rigby's Mortgage would exhaust the Whole Estate, as there was then due on that Mortgage about £. 54,500 for Principal, Interest, and Colts, and it not being probable, that both the settled and unsettled Estates would fell for that Sum, the Average Nett Yearly Income from the Whole of the then lait Seven Years being no more than about £. 1,500; and it furthtr appeared, that with a view to give Relief to the Petitioner and his Family, in Consideration of the Hardship of their Cafe, which had been entirely occasioned by an extraordinary Interpolation, of the Legislature, to their Prejudice, in consequence of the Imposition practised as before stated, the said Act was passed in the Year 1794, whereby, after reciting to the Vol. j6.

Effect aforesaid, and that the said Richard Rigby, the Mortgagee of the aforesaid Estates, died indebted to the Crown in a very large Sum of Money, of which there was then £.140,000 and upwards due; and also reciting that it had been proposed, that the Crown should, as between itself and the Representatives and Private Creditors of the said Richard Rigby, be considered as entitled to the Whole Benefit of the aforesaid Mortgage; and the said mortgaged Estates being estimated to be of the Value of £.40,000, it had been further proposed, that the Estate of the said Richard Rigby should be discharged from the Sum of £.40,000, Part of the aforesaid Debt due therefrom to the Crown, which Proposal being apprehended to be highly beneficial to the Representatives and Private Creditors of the said Richard Rigby, the same would be agreed to on their Parts; and also reciting, that the Petitioner was desirous of having the said mortgaged Estates veiled in Trust, for himself and his Family, upon his procuring to be paid into His Majesty's Exchequer, such Sum of Money as, under the aggravated Distress of his Cafe, attended with all its peculiar Circumstances, Parliament, in their Wisdom and Humanity, should think reasonable; and in order thereto the Petitioner humbly proposed, that it might be referred to the Lords Commissioners of the Treasury, to inquire into and ascertain what Sum was reasonable and proper to be paid into the Exchequer; and that upon such Payment being made, the Real and Personal Re-presentatives of the said Richard Rigby should convey the said mortgaged Estates to proper Persons, discharged from all Claims of the Personal Representatives and Private Creditors of the said Richard Rigby, and also from all Claims of the Crown, in respect of the same Estates, and also discharged from the Trulls of the aforesaid Settlement and Act of Parliament; but subject nevertheless, in thefirft place, to secure the Sum so to be paid into the Exchequer to the Lender thereof, with Interest, and then to secure to the Sifters of the Petitioner such proportionable Provision as they should be entitled to, in respect of the Portions originally secured to them upon the said settled Estates, and subject thereto, in Trust for the Petitioner in Fee Simple, it was enacted, that in same it should appear to the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty's Treasury that it would be necessary to resort to the said mortgaged Premises, in order to recover the Balance due from the said Richard Rigby to His Majesty, it should or might be lawful to and for the Lords Commissioners for executing the Office of Treasurer of His Majesty's Exchequer, or any Three or more of them, or the Lord High Treasurer, and they and he were authorized and required, to inquire and al-certain what Sum of Money would be reasonable and proper, under the Circumstances of the Cafe, to be paid into the Exchequer, in Consideration of the Crown's releasing and discharging the Estate of the said Richard Rigby from the Sum of £.40,000, Part of the Debt due to the Crown from the said Estate; and also, in Consideration of the said mortgaged Estates being veiled in proper Persons, for the Purposes aforesaid, discharged of all Claims on the Part of the Crown; and Provision is made by the said Act for effectuating the other Purposes mentioned in the Recitals thereof; and by which Act, it further appears, that in consequence of the Condition therein contained, whereby the Relief thereby given was restrained to the Cafe, " That " in case it should appear that it would be necessary to " resort to the said mortgaged Premises, in order to " recover the Balance due from the said Richard Rigby " to His Majesty," the Petitioner might have received the Benefit thereby intended; A Petition of John Adams, Woollen and Worsted Manufacturer, of Bromsgrove, in the County of Worcester, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the Bill for veiling, for a limited Time, in the Reverend Edmund Cartwright, Clerk, Mailer of Arts, his Executors, Administrators, and Assigns, the sole Property in certain Machinery by him invented fot Woolcombing; and Setting forth, That the Petitioner was not apprised of the Application for Leave to bring in the said Bill until after the same had been read a Second Time; and he finds, from the Provisions of the said Bill, that, if the same should pass into a Law, it will be very injurious to his Interests, as he will thereby be deprived of the free Use and Exercise of his own Inventions as a Woolcomber and Woollen Manufacturer; and that the Extension of the said Letters Patent will not be productive of such Advantage to the Public as the said Edmund Cartwright has set forth in his Petition: And therefore praying, That the Petitioner may be heard, by himself, or Counsel, against the said Bill, and that the same may not pass into a Law; or that he may have such Relief in the Premises as to the House shall seem meet.

A Petition of the Right honourable Lewis Lord Sondes, and the humble Petition of the several other Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed. Owners and Occupiers of Estates situate in the Eadern Division of the County of Kent,was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the Bill for repealing so much of an Act, made in the 9th Year of the Reign Vot. 36.

of King George the Second, intituled, An Act to " enable the Justices of the Peace, acting for the Western Division of the County of Kent, to purchase " a convenient Piece of Ground for building a Gaol for " the said County, and for empowering the said Justices to apply Part of the County Stock of the said Division towards the fame," as requires that the said Gaol should be repaired exclusively at the Expences of the said Western Division, and for raising the Money for repairing the same on the County at large, in Manner as other County Gaols are by Law directed to be repaired; and for empowering the Justices of the Peace for the said County, to hold an Annual General Sessions, and also a Special General Sessions, for the Purpose of making a fair and equal County Rate for the said County, and for regulating the Expenditure of the fame, and for other Purposes therein mentioned; and,

Setting forth, That the Petitioners conceive that the said Bill, if passed into a Law, will be injurious to their Rights and Interests: And therefore praying, That . they may be heard against the said Bill, by their Coun-fel, or Agents, and Witnesses, and that the same may not be passed into a Law.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, until the Report be received from the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed; and that the Petitioners be then heard, by their Counsel, Agents, and Witnesses, against the said Bill, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That Counsel be admitted to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

A Motion was made, and the Question being put, Mutioa rela-That an humble Address be presented to His Majesty, convention that He will be graciously pleated to communicate to fortheEvacu-His faithful Commons, by whose Advice, Instructions ationofEgypg (dated 15th December 1799) were given to the Commander in Chief of His Majesty's Fleet in the Mediterranean, enjoining him not to consent, on any Account, to the Return of the French Army to France, or to their,

capitulating in any other Manner than jointly to the Allied Powers, whose Forces were employed against them, or upon any other Terms than that of giving up their Arms, and surrendering as Prisoners of War to the Allied Powers so employed; and on no Account to consent to the Return of the French Army in Egypt to France, or to their capitulating, excepting on the Conditions above stipulated; whereby His faithful Commons humbly conceive that the grand Object of Peace has been postponed, and the Seat of this calamitous, unfortunate, and expensive War, has been transferred to the very distant Coasts of Egypt, where there has already been a prodigious Expenditure of Englifk Blood and English Treasure; and this at a Time when the hostile Preparations in the Ports of France threaten an Invasion of these Realms, and when our good and old Ally Portugal, is about to fink under the Dominion of the French Republic, in consequence of that Army, which might have defended Portugal,being detached to Egypt; and, moreover, when the dangerous Question of searching Neutral Ships has raised up a new War in the Baltic, and when

Prussia has seized on the Electorate of Hanover and its Treasures; and all those unfortunate and alarming Circumstances. His faithful Commons humbly conceive, grew out of the Breach of the Convention of El Arish 1 and furthermore, with the most loyal Attachment and -affectionate Confederation, His faithful Commons humbly conceive, that, by the issuing the said Instructions,a dreadful Consequence might arile to the Indian Empire,-and that it may fall into irretrievable Ruin, and, in its Fall, may crush the Credit, and destroy the Revenues of this Country; whereby, at this alarming Crisis, big with the Destinies of the whole civilized World, the Laws of Humanity, and the Laws of Nations, have beengrossly violated. His Majesty's Government degraded, and the Policy, Character, and Faith of this renowned Empire, rendered contemptible in the Eyes of all Europe,

The House divided.

A Message from the Lords, by Mr. and Mr,

Ord:

Mr, Speaker,

The Lords have commanded us to acquaint this House, That the Lords do concur in the Resolutions communicated to them at a Conference on Friday the 8th of May last; and have agreed to an Address to be presented to His Majesty thereupon; to which Address their Lordships desire the Concurrence of this House.

And then the Messengers withdrew.

Resolved, That this House will fend an Answer to that Part of the said Message, which relates to the said Address, by Messengers of their own.

And the Messengers were again called in; and Mr. Speaker acquainted them therewith.

And then they again withdrew.

The House proceeded to take the said Address into Confederation.

And the said Address was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Most Gracious Sovereign,

We, Your Majesty's most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, in Parliament assembled, humbly beg Leave to inform Your Majesty, that we have had under our Consideration the Expediency of a more speedy and general Promulgation of the Statutes; and we have come to the several Resolutions which we now humbly present to Your Majesty. And we entreat Your Majesty will be graciously pleased to give such Directions for the more speedy and general Promulgation of the Statutes of the United Kingdom, throughout all Parts of Great Britain and Ireland, as Your Majesty shall think proper.

The said Address being read a Second Time; Resolved, That this House doth agree with the Lords in the said Address to be presented to His Majesty.

And the Blank therein was filled up with the Words " and Commons."

Ordered, That a Message be sent to the Lords, to acquaint their Lordships, That this House hath agreed to the Address, to which the Lords desired the Concurrence of this House; and have filled up the Blank with the Words, "and Commons."

Ordered, That Mr. Abbot do carry the said Message.

Mr. Bragge, according to Order, reported from the Report on Im-

Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred j^rnSonof to consider of the Importation and Exportation of Cop- Copper, per, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That it is expedient, after a Time to be limited, to permit the Exportation of Copper.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That it is expedient to give Power to His Majesty, by Proclamation, or Order in Council, to prohibit the Exportation of Copper to any Place within the Limits of Europe.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the Duties now payable on the Importation of Copper Bricks, Role Copper, Copper Coin, and on all Cast Copper, and the Drawbacks now allowed on the Exportation thereof, shall cease and determine.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That a Duty of Five Shillings and Three Pence be charged upon every Hundred Weight of all Copper Bricks, Rose Copper, Copper Coin, and Cast Copper, imported into Great Britain.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That a Drawback of Five Shillings and One Penny Halfpenny be allowed on every Hundred Weight of all Copper Bricks, Rose Copper, Copper Coin, and Cast Copper, exported from. Great Britain.

The said Resolutions being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

the Petitioner, from her melancholy and unfortunate Situation, is living in a very humble and retired Manner, and hath little or no Intercourse with Society, and therefore had no Opportunity of knowing the Provisions inserted in the said Bill until this present Day; and that Hie hath been informed, that the said Bill, provides, that it shall not be lawful for her to contract a Second Marriage in the Life Time of the said Doctor James,

but that any such Marriage shall be null and void; and that the Petitioner, being left by the said Bill without any Provision for her Support, and being an Outcast from her own Family, as well as from Society in general, most humbly throws herself upon the Humanity and Companion of the House, and hopes the aforesaid Proviso may not pass into a Law, as it will deprive her of the only Possibility Ihe can have of ever being restored to a decent and comfortable Situation; and that the Petitioner hath not the Means of defraying the Expence of opposing the said Proviso by Counsel: And therefore Prays the House will be graciously pleased to take the Premises into Consideration, and grant her such Relief therein as to them shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the said Committee.

A Petition of the Freeholders, Proprietors of Old Inclosed Land, in the Parish of Louth, in the County of Lincoln, who have thereunto set their Names, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth, That the Inclosure of the small Open Fields of Louth will be of no material Advantage to the Public, or to the Town of Louth, considering that there are now more than 750 Acres of Old Incloled Meadows and Pasture Lands very contiguous to the Town; and that the Soil of these Open Fields is belt adapted for Wheat and Beans, of which it produces excellent Crops alternately, and is in a very high State of Cultivation; and there is no W'afte Land, as the Commons are a very rich Pasture, which keep a large Quantity of Cattle, the Property of a great many industrious People, who have Common Rights, and are enabled by their Common Rights to maintain their Families, and increase the Population and Prolperity of the Town of Louth: And therefore praying the House, either to re-jedl the Bill, or not to suffer that Part thereof to pass into a Law, which would compel the Petitioners to rc-linquilb Part of their Old Inclosed Land against their Consent, but permit them to remain subject to the Tythes they have hitherto paid, whichever the House may think proper.

Re-commhted Mr. Diekinson reported from the Committee, to whom Report re- the Report was re-committed, which was made from mfifioofrf&c ^ie Committee who were appointed to consider of the in inclosure Persons to be appointed Commissioners, Surveyors, and acts. Valuers, in Bills of Inclosure and Drainage, and to

report the fame, with their Opinion thereupon, to the House; That the Committee had further considered the Matter to them referred, and had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Resolutions of the Committee were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, after the present Session of Parliament, in every Bill for inclosing any Moors, Commons, Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, and in every Bill for draining any Low Lands, there be inserted a Clause or Clauses, to prevent any Lord, or the Steward, Bailiff, or Agent, or any Person who hath been Steward, Bailiff, or Agent, within the Space of Three Years previous to the Royal Assent being given to such Act, of any Lord or Lady of any Manor or Manors extending pver the Whole, or over any Part of the said Moors, Commons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, intended to be by such Bill inclosed, or Low Lands intended to be by such Bill drained; and also to prevent any Proprietor or Person, immediately interested, or the Steward, Bailiff, or Agent, or any Person who hath been Steward, Bailiff, or Agent, within the Space of Three Years previous to the Royal Assent being, given.to such Act, of any Proprietor or Person immediately interested in such Moors, Com-. ... 9

mons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, intended to be by such Bill inclosed, or Low Lands intended to be by such Bill drained; from acting as Commissioner, Surveyor, or Valuer, for the inclosing such Moors, Commons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, or for the draining such Low Lands.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, after the present Session of Parliament, in every Bill for the inclosing any Moors, Commons, or Waste Lands, Half Year Lands, or uninclosed Lands, or for the draining of any Low Lands, there be inserted an Oath or Oaths, Affirmation or Affirmations, to be taken by every Commissioner, Surveyor, and Valuer, of Lands intended to be by such Bill inclosed or drained, that he is not immediately interested in the lands so intended to be inclosed or drained, and is not Steward,

Bailiff, or Agent, and hath not been Steward, Bailiff, or Agent, of any Person so interested, within the Space of Three Years previous to the Royal Assent being given to the said Act.

Mr., Chancellor of the Exchequer acquainted the House, That he had a Message from His Majesty to this House, signed by His Majesty; and he presented the same to the House; and it was read by Mr. Speaker (all the Members of the House being uncovered); and is as followeth; viz,

GEORGE R.

As the State of Public Business may soon enable His Majesty to put an End to the present Session, His Majesty thinks it proper to recommend it to the House of Commons, to consider of making Provision to enable His Majesty to defray such Extraordinary Expences, (in Addition to those which will be incurred in fulfilling the specific Engagements which His Majesty has already directed to be laid before Parliament) and to take such Measures as the Exigency of Affairs may require.

G. R.

Ordered, That His Majesty's said most Gracious Message be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom it is referred to consider further of the Supply granted to His Majesty.
