A Petition of the Persons thereunder-signed, in Behalf of themselves and others, residing in the Town and County of Poole, and carrying on the British Fishery in the Island of Newfoundland, being offered to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That the British Fishery carried on in the llland of Newfoundland has ever been considered to be highly advantageous to the Nation, as well as beneficial to the Individuals immediately concerned in the Prole-cution of it, and has therefore been deemed worthy the Attention of the Legislature, which has, from Time to Time, by Acts of Encouragement and Protection, given it that Support which Circumstances required, and without which, no Concern depending upon adventitious Occurrences could at certain Times exist; and that the said Fishery is at the present Period an Object peculiarly worthy of the National Concern, inasmuch as it affords a valuable Nursery for Seamen, as, with proper Encouragement, it might become a Source of Individual, and consequently National Wealth, and as a certain Resource to which the Nation might always look for a never-failing Supply of wholesome and nutritive Food in every same of Emergency; and that the said Fishery is at this Time in a State of extreme Deprellion, occasioned principally by the peculiar Circumstances of the Times, in consequence of which, the Price of the various Articles of Provisions and Stores, necessary for the Prosecution of the said Fishery, are enhanced in an exorbitant Degree, while, at the same Time, those Markets,which have hitherto remained open for the Sale of the Produce, have been proportionably depressed, and by far the greatest Part of those Markets to which the Petitioners have usually resorted, have for several Years been lhut against them; and that the Petitioners, since their

The Petitioners therefore submit to the House, the Propriety, in a National Point of View, of granting such Encouragement, by way of Bounty, as, by insuring to the Petitioners a Price adequate to the Charges of taking, curing, and importing the fame, and in some Measure equal to what they have been in the Habits of obtaining in Foreign Markets, would enable them to order a Part of the Produce of the said Fishery to be brought to this Country; and the Petitioners cannot but consider this as a Measure likely to be eminently beneficial to the Nation, as well as to the Trade in which they are concerned, and entertain no Doubt, but the Consumption of the United Kingdom would, in the Course of a few Years, be equal to One-Fourth Part of the Fish caught in Newfoundland; and, in this Event, the introducing into general Use a wholesome nutritious Article of Food, of which a Supply, to almost any Extent, may be secured to the Community, may naturally be expected to have the happiest Influence in reducing and keeping down the Price of fresh Provisions in future: And therefore praying, That the House will take their same into serious

of themselves and others, refilling in the Town and County o f Poole, and carrying on the British Fisheryin

the I (land of Newfoundland, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, a Member present informed Your Committee, That the British Fishery, carried on in the Island of Newfoundland, has ever been considered to be highly advantageous to the Nation, as well as beneficial to the Individuals immediately concerned in the Prosecution of it; and has therefore been deemed worthy the Attention of the Legifla-ture, which has from Time to Time, by Acts of Encouragement and Protection, given it that Support which Circumstances required, and without which no Concern depending upon adventitious Occurrences, could at certain Times exist: That the said Fishery is at the present Period, an Object peculiarly worthy of the National Concern, inasmuch as it affords a valuable Nursery for Seamen, as, with proper Encouragement, it might become a Source of Individual, and consequently National Wealth, and as a certain Resource to which the Nation might always look for a never-failing Supply of wholesome and nutritive Food in every Cale of Emergency: That the said Fishery is at this Time in a State of extreme Deprefiion, occasioned principally by the peculiar Circumstances of the Times, in consequence of which, the Price of the various Articles of Provisions and Stores, ne-celfary for the Prosecution of the said Fishery, arc enhanced in an exorbitant Degree, while at the same Time, those Markets which have hitherto remained open for the Sale of the Produce, have been proportionably deprelfed; and by far the greatest Part of those Markets, to which the Petitioners have usually resorted, have for several Years been Ihut against them: That the Petitioners, since their Exclusion from the Ports of Spain and , have been accustomed to fend the Produce of the said Fishery to the Ports of Portugal, where the Markets being overstocked, they have experienced such heavy Sales as have occasioned great Loss: That the Petitioners now view with Concern the Profpelt of the Markets of Portugal being also Ihut against them, when they shall have no other Resource than the West India Hlands, and the United States of America, whole joint Consumption bearing no Proportion to the Produce of the Fishery, they mull consequently be burthened with a large undif-pofabie Property; and even should their Fears with regard to Portugal,prove unfounded, still the Petitioners,

risking large Properties with very Header Profpclls of any suitable Returns, shall need the supporting Aid of the Legislature, and without it, will in all Probability be eventually compelled to abandon the Trade: That the Petitioners have good Reason to believe, from the Experience of the last Winter, in the Course of which a considerable Quantity of Dry Cod Fish was consumed by the lower and middling Claflfesof the Community in the Western Parts of the Kingdom, that this Country ' would take off Annually a considerable Quantity of that Article, provided it could be rendered at reasonable Prices; the Petitioners would therefore humbly submit to the House the Propriety, in a National point of View, of granting such Encouragement, by Way of Bounty, as by insuring to the Petitioners a Price adequate to the Charges of taking, curing, and importing, the fame, and in some Measure equal to what they have beeu in the Habits of obtaining in Foreign Markets, would enable them to order a Part of the Produce of the said Fishery to be brought to this Country; and the Petitioners consider this as a Measure likely to be eminently beneficial to the Nation, as well as to the Trade in which they are concerned, and entertain no Doubt but the Consump-

Setting forth, That, by the Direction of a considerable Number of Persons residing or having Property in, the Neighbourhood of the said Road., the usual Steps were taken preparatory to an Application to Parliament for an Act to amend the said Road, and a Bill was drawn by an Agent in the Country, which was, at a Meeting, submitted to the Consideration of the Promoters of the Plan, and to the Persons who had subscribed divers large Sums of Money to be applied in the Amendment and Repair of the said Road, under the Authority of the proposed Act; and that the Bill so drawn was by them approved, and presented to the House, where it is now depending; and that one of the principal Objects of the said Bill is to open a Communication by which the adjoining Country may be supplied with Lime for general Uses, and more especially for the Purposes of Agriculture; and, as it was well known that the Road could not be maintained, or the Interest of the Money so to be advanced be paid, without a Toll on Lime generally, that Article was excepted in the Clause giving the other Exemptions usually inserted in Turnpike Acts; and that the Petitioners are informed that the

Setting forth, That the present Method of filling Wheat and other Grain by Measure, in which no regular Standard is used, is productive of great Inconvenience and Deception, and renders it importable to ascertain the real Price of such Wheat and Grain, as it is found to be impracticable, under the existing Laws, to guard against the Frauds praftited in the Returns made to the Clerk of the Market; and consequently, the Mngilb-ates are unable to fix the Assize of Bread from those Returns with any Correctnds, in Proportion to the real Average Price of Corn; and that the Petitioners, and the Public in general, labour under great Imposition in con-ilquence of the present Method of felling Potatoes, Turnips, Carrots, and Parships, by Mc^-sure; and it would tend greatly to the Benefit of the Public, and to remedy the Evils now experienced, it Wheat, and all other Corn, and also Potatoes, Turnips, Carrots, and Parsnips, were sold by one fixed Weight only: And therefore praying, That the House will take the above Evils into Consideration, and provide such Remedy as shall fieem meet.

Distillers and Makers of Spirits, in that Part of the United Kingdom called England, was presented to the House, and read; Settingfdrth, That, by the Act for the Union of Great Britain and Ireland, certain Provisions are made respecting Countervailing Duties, and by virtue thereof the Exporter of Spirits from Ireland to England is entitled to a Drawback of the Duty . paid on Spirits in Ireland-, and, by an Act of the last Session of the Parliament of Ireland, intituled, "An Act " to encourage the Distillation of Spirits from Sugar,

" for a limited Time," is also entitled to a Drawback of the Duty paid upon the Sugar from which such Spirits are at present made, being Nineteen Shillings and Seven Pence the Hundred Weight; and that no Countervailing Duty being imposed by the said last mentioned Act, in respect of the said Drawback upon the Sugar from which such Spirits are made in Ireland, the Distiller actually imports his Spirits into England at lo much less Rate of Duty than the English Distiller pays, as Nineteen Shillings and Seven Pence the Hundred Weight in the Raw Material, or about Two Shillings per Gallon on the Spirits, than is paid by the Petitioners, and is thereby enabled contidcrably to under-fell them;

.and that by Reason thereof, large Quantities of Spirits have been imported into England from Ireland, and the Petitioners have every Keafon to apprehend that con- fulerable Quantities of Spirits in Ireland, now in Rcadi-ness, will be shipped, and arrive under similar Circumstances, to the Detriment of the Revenue, and the great Injury of the Petitioners, who have at this Time such large Quantities in Hand as that the Duties paid thereon exceed f.zoo,coo, and for which they have, for the Reasons before mentioned, at present no Demand; And therefore praying, That such an additional Countervailing Duty per Gallon may be imposed upon Spirits imported into England, as will bear a fair Proportion to the Drawback of Nineteen Shillings and Seven Pence the Hundred Weight allowed upon the Sugar; and ir.af-much as the hid Act of Union directs, that, when any new or additional Countervailing Duty shall be imposed on the Import of any Article into either Country from the other, a Drawback equal in Amount to such Countervailing Duty shall be given in like Manner on the Export of every such Article respectively from the same Country to the other; and that a Drawback may be allowed to the Engl ijhDistiller upon the Exportation of Spirits to Ireland, equal in Amount to any such additional Countervailing Duty, in order that the English and Irish Distillers may export to the respective Countries

A Petition of Robert O'Hara, of the City of Dublin, Esquire, Pursuivant of His Majesty's Court of Exchequer, in that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, was also presented to the House, and read; likewise Taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth, That the Petitioner, in the Year 1781, was, by His Majesty's Letters Patent, under the Great Seal of Ireland, appointed Pursuivant of the said Court of Exchequer, and has ever since, and now enjoys, the said Office, and executes the same by hithfelf and his Deputy; and that the Petitioner and his Deputy are entitled to, and have received, and do receive, considerable Fees and Profits in the said Office, which arise On Attachments awarded and directed to them for Contempts in the Non-performance of the Orders, and the Non-execution or Abuse of the Process and Executions in the several Suits instituted in the said Court of Exchequer, in Personal Actions; and that the Petitioner will suffer a considerable Diminution of his Fees and Profits of the said Office, if the said Bill should pass into a Law; and his said Office of Pursuivant is not mentioned in the said Act, as one of those the Officer of which should receive Compensation on Account of the Loss and Diminution of his Fees and Profits, although he is, and has been as aforesaid, an Officer of the said Court for Twenty Years last past: And therefore praying. That the House will take his same into Consideration; and, in the Event of the Bill being passed into a Law, to insert his said Office of Pursuivant therein, as one of those the Officer of which shall be entitled to Compensation, on Account of the Diminution of the said Fees and Emoluments.

A Petition of Daniel Beere, of the City of Dublin, Gentleman, Deputy Pursuivant of His Majesty's Court of Exchequer in that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, was likewise presented to the House, and read; also Taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth, That the Petitioner, in the Year 1781, was appointed Deputy Pursuivant of the said Court of Exchequer, to exercise and conduct the Duty and Buli-ness thereof, and he has ever since accordingly exercised and conducted the said Business, and still continues so to do sand that the Petitioner is intitled to considerable Fees and Profits in the said Office; and, if the said Bill should pass into a Law, the Business of the said Court of Exchequer will be very considerably leficned, and the Petitioner will in consequence thereof, suffer a considerable Diminution of his Fees and Profits: And therefore praying, That the House will take his same into Consideration; and, in the Event of the said Bill being passed into a Law, to insert his said Office of Deputy Pursuivant of the said Court of Exchequer therein, so that the Petitioner may be considered one of those Officers of the said Court entitled to Gom-pensation.

Report on Mr. Nicholas Vanjittart reported from the Committee, to the&lt ng appointed to enquire into the Laws relating to the Salt Duties. Duties, and the Means of remedying the Incon-

veniences arising therefrom, and to report the fame, with their Opinion thereupon, from Time to Time, to the House; That the Committee had proceeded in the Matters to them referred, and had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Resolutions of the Committee were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, for promoting and encouraging the Fisheries of the United Kingdom, and for the Relief of the Merchants and Agents concerned in procuring and supplying Salt for the fame, it is expedient that Bond, or

Security, should be taken for the due Delivery of such Salt in the Single Value of the Duty only.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, in all Cases in which any Salt shall be shipped or delivered. Duty-free, for the Use of the Fisheries, it shall be lawful for the Principal Officer of Excise at the Port at which such Salt shall be so shipped or delivered, to accept the Bond of any sufficient and responfibte Person, to be approved of by such Officer.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, in all Cases in which the Deficiency of any Dutyfree Salt delivered to the Fisheries, or carried Coastwise,

shall not exceed One pet Centum of the Weight of such Salt, such Deficiency shall be allowed as unavoidable Waste, on Proof that it has not been occasioned by Fraud or Embezzlement.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That Six Months shall be allowed for the Production of Certificates for cancelling or discharging Bonds granted for the due Delivery of Duty-free Salt.

The First Resolution of the Committee being read a Second Time, was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

The Second Resolution of the Committee being read a Second Time, several Amendments were proposed to be made thereunto, by leaving out, after the Words " Bond of" the Word " any," and by leaving out the Word "Person" and inserting the Word "Persons" instead thereof.

And the said Amendments were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Resolved, That this House doth agree with the Committee in the said Resolution, so amended, That in all Cases in which any Salt shall be shipped or delivered.

Duty-free, for the Use of the Fisheries, it shall be lawful for the Principal Officer of Excise at the Port at which such Salt shall be so shipped or delivered, to accept the Bond of sufficient and responsible Persons, to be approved of by such Officer.

The subsequent Resolutions of the Committee, being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Mr. Bragge, according to Order, reported from the Report on Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred commerce to consider of the Treaty of Commerce concluded between with America. His Majesty and the United States of America, the Refo lutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth;

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee*

That it is expedient to permit any Goods, Wares, or Merchandize, the Produce or Manuf acture of the United States of America, which are not prohibited by Law to be imported from Foreign Countries, to be imported into Ireland directly from any of the Territories of the said United States, in Ships of the Built of the United Kingdom, owned, navigated, and registered according to Law, or in Ships built in the Countries belonging to the said States, or in Ships taken by any Vessels be* longing to the Government or Inhabitants thereof, and condemned there as lawful Prize, and owned by the Subjects of the said States, and whereof the Master

9° yu

A, 1801.

5 9*

and Three-fourths of the Mariners are Subjects of the said States.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient to permit all such Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, not being prohibited, which (half be imported into Ireland from the said States, either in Ships of the Built of the United Kingdom, or of the said United States, to be entered and landed, upon Payment bf such Duties of Customs and Excise as are payable on Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, of the like Denomination or Description, upon their Importation into Ireland in any such Ships respectively from any other Foreign Country; and where different Duties are imposed upon the Importation of any such Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, from different Foreign Countries, then Upon Payment of the lowest Duties now payable on the Importation in Ships of the Built of the United Kingdom of any such Goods, Wares, or Merchandize, from any Foreign Country now in Amity with His Majesty.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient to permit Pig Iron, Bar Iron, Pitch, Tar, Tobacco, Turpentine, Rosin, Pot Ash, Pearl Ash, Mahogany, Mails, Yards, and Bowsprits, being the Growth, Production, or Manufacture, of the said States, and all Staves, and ' unmanufactured Goods and Merchandize, which are not prohibited by Law to be imported from Foreign Countries, being the Growth or Production of the said States, to be imported into Ireland, in Ships of the Built of the United Kingdom, or of the said United States, on Payment of such Duties of Customs and Excise as are payable on the like Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, upon their Importation into Iceland, in Ships of the Built of the United Kingdom, from any British I Hand or Plantation in.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, upon the Importation into Ireland from the United States of Ameriea of Wheat, Wheat Meal or Flour, Rye, Barley, Beer or Bigg, Oats, Oatmeal, Pease, Beans, Indian Corn, and Maize, the Duties to be paid thereon shall be regulated according to the Prices of Wheat, Rye, Barley, Beer or Bigg, Pease, Beans, Oats, and Oatmeal, specified according to an Act, passed in the Parliament of Ireland, in the 31st Year of His present Majesty's Reign.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient to permit Oil, made from Fish or Creatures living in the Sea, and Blubber, Whale Fins, and Spermaceti, being the Produce of the Fisheries carried on by the People of the said United States, to be imported into Ireland from the said States, in Ships of the Built of the United Kingdom, or of the said United States, on Payment of such Duties of Customs as are payable on the like Articles, upon their Importation into Ireland, in Ships of the United Kingdom, from Countries not under the Dominion of His Majesty.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Tobacco, being the Growth or Production of the said United States, be permitted to be imported into Ireland in Ships of the United Kingdom, or in American Ships, upon Payment of the like Duties as Tobacco imported by British Subjects from any British Colony or Plantation in America, shall be subject to; and that Snuff, being the Production and Manufacture of any of the said Territories, be permitted to be imported into Ireland upon Payment of the like Duties as Snuff, the Production or Manufacture of Europe, imported from Europe, shall be lubject to.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Rice, the Produce of the said United States, be permitted to be landed and warehoused in Ireland, under certain Regulations and Restrictions.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it isexpedient that Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, imported from the said State* into An shall, upon'

the Exportation thereof to any Foreign Country, be entitled to the same Drawbacks as shall be allowed upon the Exportation of Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, of the like Denomination, when exported from Ireland to any Foreign Country; and that the like Bounties and Drawbacks be allowed on Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, exported from Ireland to the Territories of the said States, as shall be allowed upon the Exportation of Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, of the like Denomination, exported to any British Colony or Plantation in America.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient, that the like Drawbacks be allowed upon the Exportation from Ireland of Foreign Hemp or Foreign Iron, exported to any British Colony or Plantation in America, or to the Territories of the said States, as shall be allowed upon the Exportation of the like Sort of Hemp or Iron to other Foreign Parts.

The said llefolutions being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

A Clause was offered to be added to the Bill, for making Compensation for the Tythes of Allotments sold to defray the Expences of the Act.

And the said Clause was Twice read; and, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House, to be made Part of the Bill.

Mr. Bragge reported from the Committee, appointed Report on to take into Consideration the Standing Orders of this House relative to Bills of Inclosure, and to report the to JiicJolurc

lame,

1

fame, with their Opinion thereupon, and who were empowered to report, from Time to Time, to the House; That the Committee had considered the Matters to them referred, and had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Resolutions of the Committee were read, and are as followed; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, in all Bills for inclosing Lands or Commons, which shall be presented to the House after this Session of Parliament, there be inserted a Clause, providing what Sum of Money, in the Whole, shall be paid to each of the Commissioners to be appointed by such Bill, in full Satisfaiflion of the Expence and Trouble which he Avail incur in the Execution of the Trusts and Powers thereby given; or that, in Default of such Provision being made, there be inserted a Clause providing that the Account of such Commissioner or Commissioners, containing a true Statement of all Sums by him or them received and expended, or due to him or them for their own Trouble or Expences, shall, at lead once in every Year, from the Date of the passing of such Act till such Accounts shall be finally allowed, together with the Vouchers relating to the fame, be examined by some Person or Persons in such Bill to be named, and the Balance by him or them dated in the Book of Accounts already required to be kept in the Office of the Clerk of such Commissioners; and that no Charge or Item in such Accounts shall be binding on the Parties concerned, or be valid in Law, unless the same shall be duly allowed by such Person or Persons.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That in all such Bills as above mentioned, Provision be made that no Witness summoned to attend such Commissioner or Commissioners shall be obliged to travel above Eight Miles from the Boundary of the Parish, Manor, or District, thereby intended to be inclosed.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That in all such Bills, Provision be made for empowering and requiring the Commissioner or Commissioners named in such Bills, to appoint One or more Surveyor or Surveyors, with or without a Salary, for the fird forming and completing such Parts of the public Carriage Roads dire died to be set out and appointed by such Bill, as shall be newly made, and for putting into complete Repair such Part of the same as shall have been previously made, and for defraying the Expence of such Salary, and of forming, completing, and repairing, such Roads respectively, over and above a Proportion of the Statute Duty on the Roads to be so repaired, either by Sale of a sufficient Portion of the said Lands, or by a Rate to be settled and apportioned by such Commissioner or Commissioners, upon the Owners and Proprietors of the fame; and in case of Sale of such Lands, for the Payment of the Produce thereof, before the Execution of the Award to such Surveyor or Surveyors, to be accounted for as herein after directed, and for making a conditional Rate upon such Owners and Proprietors, in case the Produce of such Sale should prove insufficient for the Purposes aforesaid, and for subjccting such Surveyor or Surveyors, and his or their Accounts, to the Jurisdiction and Controul of the Justices of the Peace in all Respects whatever, and with the same Powers of levying such Rate, as may by such Justices be thought necessary, according to the Proportions previously ascertained by such Commissioner or Commissioners, in like Manner as if he or they had been appointed by virtue of the General Highway Act, passed in the 13th Year of His present Majesty, and for the Re-payment of any Surplus that may remain in his or their Hands after such Roads shall be completely formed and repaired, to such Persons as shall have been made liable to contribute thereto, according to the Proportions above mentioned, 6

and for preventing any Charge or Burthen being laid on the Inhabitants at large, except such Proportion of such Statute Duty as aforesaid, until the same shall, by such Justices in their Special Sessions, be so ordered or directed; and for enforcing, by certain Penalties on such Surveyor or Surveyors to be specified in such Bill, the completing and repairing such Roads within Two Years after the said Award, unless such Justices shall, on fufii-cient Cause being altedged and proved to their Satisfaction, grant a further Time, not exceeding One Year.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That in all such Bills, whenever any Sum of Money is under the Provisions of such Bill, to be paid for the Pun* chafe or Exchange of any Lands, Tenements, or Hereditaments, or of any 'l imber or Wood growing thereon, and which Sum of Money ought to be laid out in the Purchase of other Lands, Tenements, or Hereditaments, to be settled to the same Uses, Provision shall be made for empowering the Commissioner or Commissioners named in such Bill, out of such Sum to defray such Pn> portion of the Expence of passing such Act, and carrying the same into Execution, as shall, if any, be charged upon any of the Lands, Tenements, or Hereditaments* of the Person or Persons, Body Politic or Corporate, Trustees, or Feoffees, in Possession of the Lands, Tenements, or Hereditaments, so fold or exchanged, or on which such Timber or Wood actually grew, and also the Expence of any permanent Improvement, such as building, subdividing, draining, or planting, and the like, which shall in the Judgment of such Commissioner or Commissioners be proper to be made, and shall be made, under his or their Direction, upon any Lands to be by virtue of such Bill allotted to such Person or Persons, Body Politic or Corporate, Trustees or Feoffees, respectively; and that the Surplus thereof, not being less than the Sum of Two Hundred Pounds, be paid into the Bank of England, in the Name, and with the Privity, of the Accountant General of the Court of Chancery, to be placed to his Account, Parte the Commissioner or Commissioners under such particular Bill, or under such other Title as by the said Bill shall be directed, pursuant to the Method prescribed by the Act of the 12th Year of King George the First, Chapter 32. and the General Orders of the said Court, and without Fee or Reward, and shall, when so paid in, there remain until the same shall, by Order of the said Court, upon a Petition to be preferred to the said Court in a summary Way, be applied either in the Purchase of Land Tax, or towards the Discharge of any Debts or Incumbrances affecting the said Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, so purchased or exchanged, or until the same shall, upon the like Application, be laid out, in a summary Way, after allowing for the Expences necessarily attending such Purchase, by Order of the said Court, in the Purchase of other Lands, Tenements, or Hereditaments, to be settled to the like Ufesj and in the mean Time, and until such Money may, by Order of the said Court, be laid out in some of the Public Funds,or in Government or Real Securities, and the Dividends or Interest arising therefrom shall, by Order of the said Court, be paid to such Person or Persons as would, for the Time being, be entitled to the Rents and Profits of such Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments so to be purchased, conveyed, and settled: And in case such Sum of Money shall be less than the Sum of Two Hundred Pounds, and shall exceed the Sum of Twenty Pounds, then, and in such Case, such Sum of Money shall, with the Approbation of such Commissioner or Commissioners, be paid into the Bank of England, and applied, by Order of the Court of Chancery, in Manner hereinbefore directed, or may, without any Order of the Court of Chancery, be paid into the Hands of Two Trustees, to be nominated by the Person or Persons who, for the Time being, would be entitled to the Rents and Profits of the Lands, Tenements* and

Hereditaments,

Hereditaments, so to be purchased and settled, fitch Nomination to beapproved of by such Commissioner or Commissioners, and such Nomination and Approbation to be in Writing, under the Hands of the Person so nominating and approving, and the Money so paid to such Trustees shall, by them, be applied in like Manner as is before directed with Respect to the Money so to be paid into the Bank, in the Name of the Accountant General of the Court of Chancery, but without any Order of the said Court touching the Application thereof} and in case such Sum of Money thall not exceed Twenty Pounds, then the same shall be paid to the Person or Persons who, for the Time being, would be entitled to the Rents and Profits of the Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, so to be purchased and conveyed for his, her, or their own Use and Benefit.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That no Person shall be named in any such Bills as a Commissioner, Surveyor, or Valuer, who shall be inte-refled in the Inclosure to be made by virtue of such Bill, or the Agent ordinarily intruded with the Care, Superintendence, or Management, of the Estate of any Person fointercfted.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That in all such Bills there be inserted a Clause, by which the Commissioner or Commissioners shall be required to set out the public Carriage Roads in such Directions as shall, upon the Whole, appear to him or them most commodious for the Public, and to al'certain the same by Marks and Bounds, and to prepare a Map in which such intended Roads shall be accurately laid down and described, Inch Map, signed by the Commissioner, if only One, or the major Part of the said Commissioners, to be deposited with the Clerk of the said Commissioner or Commissioners; and, as soon as may be after such Carriage Roads shall have been so set out, and such Map so deposited, to give Notice in some Newl'paper to be named, circulating within that Part of ,the County where such intended Inclosure shall lie; which Notice shall also be affixed upon the Church Door of the Parish, of his or their having set out such Roads, and deposited such Map, and also of the general Lines of such intended Carriage Roads; and to appoint, in the same Notice, a Meeting to be held by the said Commissioner or Commissioners, at some convenient Place in or near to the Parish or Township within which the Inclosure is to be nude, and not iooner than Three Weeks from , the Date of such Notice, at which Meeting any Person who may be injured or aggrieved by the letting out of such Roads, may attend; and if any Person shall object. to the setting out of the lame, that then the Commissioner or Commissioners, together with any Justice or Justices of the Peace acting in and for the Division in which such Inclosure shall be made, and not being interallied in the fame, who may attend such Meeting, shall hear and determine such Objection, and the Objections of any other such Person, to any Alteration that the said Commissioner or Commissioners, Justice or Justices, may in consequence propole to make, and shall, according to their Judgment upon the Whole, order, and finally direct, how such Carriage Roads shall be set out, and either confirm the said Map, by resigning the fame, or make such Alterations therein, as the Calc may require; and in case such Commissioner or Commissioners shall by such Bill be empowered to flop up any old oraccustomed Road passing through any Part of the old Inclosures in such Parish, Township, or Place, the same shall in no same be done without the Concurrence and Order of Two Justices of the Peace acting in and for such Division, and not interested in the Repair of such Roads, and be subject to an Appeal to the Quarter Sessions, in like Manner as if the same was originally ordered by such Justices as aforesaid.

Ordered, That the said Report be taken into further Consideration upon Wednesiay Morning next.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee That there be Twenty-one Days at least between the First and Second Reading of every Private Bill relating to Ireland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, before any Petition be presented to this House for confirming or prolonging the Term of Letters Patent, granted by His Majesty to any Person or Persons, on Account of any Invention, Notice of such intended Application shall be inserted Three Times in I'he London Gazette (and also Three Times in one of the Edinburgh Papers, where the Letters Patent extend to Scotland, and also Three Times in "The Dublin Gazette, where the Letters Patent extend to Ireland) in the Months of August and September, or either of them, immediately preceding the Session of Parliament in which such Application is intended to be made; and that such Notice shall have prefixed to it, in Capital Letters, the Name by which the Invention is usually distinguished, and ilnll contain a distinct Description of the Invention for which such Letters Patent have been obtained, and also an Account of the Term of their Duration; and that the Chairman of the Committee, to whom the Petition for confirming or prolonging the Term of such Letters Patent, is referred, do report to the House how tar the Order contained in the said Resolutioa has been complied with.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, before any Bid of Divorce for Adultery do pass this House, Evidence be given before the Committee to whom the said Bill shall be committed, that an Action for Damages has been brought in One of His Majesty's Courts of Record at Westminster, or in One of His Majesty's Courts of Record in Dublin, against the Persons supposed to be guilty of Adultery, and Judgment had thereupon; or sufficient Cause be shewn to the said Committee, why such Action was not brought, or such Judgment was not obtained.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That all Persons concerned in Interest in Private Bills relating to that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland,do personally attend the Committee to give their Confcnts, or do signify the same to One of the Judges of that Part of the United Kingdom, whole Certificate shall be taken as Proof of such Content, unless the Committee, to whom any Petition or Private Bill shall be referred, shall otherwise order.

The Lords have agreed to the First and Second Amendments made by the Commons to the Bill, intituled, An Act for the Relief of certain Insolvent Debtors; but that, as to the last of the said Amendments made by the Commons to the said Bill, the Lords have disagreed thereto; and directed us to offer the following Beafons for disagreeing to the fame:

Because their Lordships are not aware of any Hard-ftiip or Inconvenience having ensued from the Law as it now stands; on the other Hand, it appears to their Lordships, that requiring the Consent of Four-fifths of the Creditors in Number and Value, is a just, expedient, and necessary Controul over the Conduct of the Bankrupt:

Because the Conduct of the Bankrupt, antecedent to the issuing the Commission, may, in many Cafes, with great Justice, be taken into the Consideration of allowing his Discharge.

And the Question being put. That this House doth insist upon the Amendment made by this House, to which the Lords have disagreed;

Mr. Fraggereported from the Committee, appointed

to take into Consideration the Standing Orders of this House, relative to Bills of Inclosure, and to report the fame, with their Opinion thereupon; and who were Vo 1. 56.

empowered to report, from Time to Time, to the House; That the Committee had further considered the Matters to them referred, arid had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; and lie read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where' the Resolutions of the Committee were read; and areas followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Two Standing Orders of the House, of the 15th Day of April 1774, and One of the 15th Day of November 1775, relating to Bills of Inclosure, should continue in horcc.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the First St anding Order of the House, of the 14th Day of March 1781, that of the 3d Day of March 1800, the Secon.l, Third, Fourth, and Sixth of the Orders agreed to by the House on Monday last, relating to Bills of Inclosure, should be limited in their Construction, so as only to prevent any such Bill from containing Clauses contrary to any such Orders respectively.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That all Persons concerned in Interest in any Bill for inclosing any Lands or Grounds, or for extinguishing any Right of Common therein, may signify their Consent to the same by Affidavit, taken and authenticated according to the Form prescribed in the Schedule to a Bill, intituled, "An Act for consolidating, in One " Act, certain Provisions usually inserted in Acts of " Inclosure, and for facilitating the Mode of proving " the several Fasts usually required on the parting of " such Acts," unless the Committee, to whom the Petition or Bill for such Inclosure or Improvement shall be referred, shall otherwise order.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Committee, to whom any Petition or Bill for the inclosing any Lands or Grounds, or for extin. guishing any Right of Common thereon, shall be referred, may admit Proof of the Notices required by the Standing Orders of this House, and of the Allega* tions in the Preamble of such Bill, by Affidavit, taken and authenticated according to the Form prescribed in the Schedule to the said Bill, unless such Committee shall otherwise order.

Resolved, That it js the Opinion of this Committee, That the Three last Resolutions shall not take Effect, unless the said Bill shall pass into a Law.

Ordered, That the said Report be taken into further Consideration Tomorrow Morning.

And then the House adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

Second Re- Mr. Nicholas Vansittart reported from the Committee relating to The appointed to enquire into the Laws relating to the SaltDuties. Salt Duties, and the Means of remedying the Incon-

veniences arising therefrom, and to report the fame, with their Opinion thereupon, from Time to Time, to the House; That the Committee had made a further Progress in the Matters to them referred, and had directed him to make a Report thereof, together with Vox,. 56.

several Resolutions thereupon, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered the fame, with an Appendix thereunto, in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Report was read; and the . Resolutions of the Committee are as followeth;

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That a Commutation of the Duties on Salt would be productive of many great and important Advantages to all Descriptions of Persons in this Kingdom, and would be highly beneficial to its Agriculture, Fisheries,

Trade, and Manufactures.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That such a Commutation can only be effected by some general Tax, extending, as far as Circumstances will admit, to all the Orders of the Community, all of whom would derive Benefit from such Commutation.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That it is expedient to postpone the further Consideration of this Subject until the next Session of Parliament.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That such a Number of Copies of the said Report, with the Appendix, be printed, as shall be sufficient for the Use of the Members of the House.

The said Report is preserved amongst the other Papers of this Session.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Resolution, made upon the said 23th April 1774, " That, when any Petition is presented to this " House for making a Navigable Canal, or for making or " improving the Navigation of a River, or for making " a new Turnpike Road, or for railing any further Sum " of Money for any of those Purposes, there be annexed " to the said Petition an Estimate of the proposed Expence of such Undertaking, signed by the Person or Persons making the same, together with an Account of the " Money subscribed for carrying the said Work into " Execution, and the Names of the Subfctibers, with the " Sums respectively subscribed by them," so far as the same relates to Turnpike Roads, be extended to Ireland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Resolution, made upon the 17th 1797, " That the precise Duration of every new temporary Law should be expressed in the Title of the " Bill, and also in a distinct Clause at the End of the " Bill, and no where else," be extended to Ireland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Resolution, made upon the said 17th November 1797, " That, where the Revival of several expired " Statutes, or the Continuance of several expiring " Statutes, is proposed, all such as are to be revived " should be included in One Bill, and such as are to " be continued in another; and that every Bill for the " Revival of several Statutes, or for the Continuance of " several Statutes, should express in its Title every " such Statute by its Year, Chapter, and Day of passing, " together with the precile Duration to be given " thereto," be extended to Ireland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Order, made upon the 3d March 1800, " That " in all Bills of Inclosure, there be inserted a Clause, " compelling the Commissioners to keep at the Office " of their Clerk a Book of Accounts open at all reasonable Times during the Progress of the Inclosure, and " till the Accounts are finally settled, for the Inspection " of any of the Proprietors, which Book shall contain " an Entry of the Particulars of all Sums of Money raised " or expended by virtue of any Powers granted by the " Ad, under a Penalty on such Commissioners or their " Clerk for neglecting or refuting the same: And also " a Clause, providing that all Monies to be raised under, " and by virtue of the Powers contained in such Ad, " Hull, as often as the same shall amount to the Sum " of Fifty Pounds, be paid into the Hands of some " Banker, or of such other Person or Persons as shall be " approved by a Majority in Value of such Proprietors " who shall be present at the First Meeting of the said " Commissioners; and in the Notice of which Meeting " shall be expressed the Intention of then appointing such Banker, or such other Person or Persons; and " and that no Monies be issued out of the Hands of " such Banker, or other Person or Persons, without an " Order of the Commissioners, specifying the Person to " whom the same are payable, and the Service for which " the same are due, and that the Balance (if any,) upon " the final Settlement of Accounts, shall be immediately " re-paid to the Land Owners, in Proportion to the " Sums respectively paid by them: And also, a Clause, " providing that the Award shall be read and executed " by the Commissioners in the Presence of the Proprietors, who may attend at a Special General Meeting called for that Purpose, of which Ten Days Notice *c at least shall be given in some Newspaper to be named, circulating within the County, which Execution of " such Award shall be proclaimed the next Sunday in the Parish Church, from the Time of which Procla- mation only, and not before, such Award shall be considered as complete," be extended to Ireland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be Twenty-one Days, at least, between the 2

First and Second Reading of every Private Bill relating to Ireland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, before any Petition be presented to this House, for confirming or prolonging the Term of Letters Patent granted by His Majesty to any Person or Persons on Account of any Invention, Notice of such intended Application shall be inserted Three Times in The London Gazette (and also Three Times in one of the Edinburgh Papers, where the Letters Patent extend to Scotland, and also Three Times in The Dublin Gazette, where the Letters Patent extend to Ireland) in the Months of August and September, or either of them, immediately preceding the Session of Parliament in which such Application is intended to be made; and that such Notice shall have prefixed to it in Capital Letters the Name by which the Invention is usually distinguished, and shall contain a distinct Description of the Invention for which such Letters Patent have been obtained, and also an Account of the Term of their Duration; and that the Chairman of the Committee, to whom the Petition for confirming or prolonging the Term of such Letters Patent is referred, do report to the House how far the Order contained in the said Resolution has been complied with.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, before any Bill of Divorce for Adultery do pass this House, Evidence be given before the Committee to whom the said Bill shall be committed, that an Action for Damages has been brought in one of His Majesty's Courts of Record at Westminster, or in one of His Majesty's Courts of Record in Dublin, against the Persons supposed to be guilty of Adultery, and Judgment had thereupon; or sufficient Cause be shewn to the said Committee, why such Action was not brought, or such Judgment was not obtained.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That all Persons concerned {in Interest in Private Bills relating to that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, do personally attend the Committee to give their Consents, or do signify the same to one of the Judges of that Part of the United Kingdom, whose Certificate shall be taken as Proof of such Consent, unless the Committee, to whom any Petition or Private Bill shall be referred, shall otherwise order.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That in all Private Bills relating to that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, the Notices required by the Standing Orders of this House, and the Allegations in the Preamble of such Bills, may be proved before any Judge of that Part of the United Kingdom, whose Certificate shall be admitted as Evidence of such Proof having been made, unless the Committee, to whom any Petition or Private Bill shall be referred, shall otherwise order.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, when any Petition for a Turnpike Road, or for eredtinga Bridge, or for paving, lighting, cleansing, or improving any Town or City, or for renewing or altering any Act of Parliament passed for those Purposes, or for inclosing, draining, or improving, any Lands, Fens, or Commons, shall have been presented to this House, the Committee to whom the said Petition shall be referred, or in case such Petition shall not be referred to a Committee, then the Committee to whom the Bill for those Purposes shall be committed, do examine, in the First Place, how far the several Orders of the House hereinbefore mentioned, viz. the Four First above referred to as being made on the 25tho 1774, the

Two on the 23d of May 1786, and the Two on the 20th May 1791, have been respectively complied with; and the Chairman of such Committee shall report the same to the House on the Report of such Petition or Bill.

" House after this Session of Parliament, Provision be " made for empowering and requiring the Commissioners named in such Bills to appoint One or more Surveyor or Surveyors, with a Salary, for the first forming, " and also putting into good and sufficient Repair the " public Carriage Roads, and for defraying the Expence " of such Salary, and of such Forming and Repair, " which shall be incurred over and above the Statute " Duty, either by Sale of a sufficient Portion of the " said Lands, or by a Rate upon the Owners and Proprietors of the Lands so inclosed within the said " Parish, and for preventing any Charge or Burthen " being laid on the Inhabitants, not being Owners or " Proprietors of Lands, towards the first: forming, " making, and repairing the said Roads, other than the " Statute Duty, until the same shall by the said Commissioners, or the said Surveyor or Surveyors, be certilled before the Justices at their Quarter Session for " the County in which such Parish shall lie, to be completely formed and made good; which Certificate the " laid Commissioners, or the said Surveyor or Surveyors, " shall be obliged to deliver to the said Justices, within " Two Years after the Award, or give sufficient Reasons " for further Allowance of Time, not exceeding One " other Year, under certain Penalties to be specified in the said Bills respectively," be repealed.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That all Persons concerned in Interest in any Bill for inclosing any Lands or Grounds, or for extinguishing any Right of Common therein, may signify their Consent to the same by Affidavit taken and authenticated according to the Form prescribed in the Schedule to a Bill, intituled, "An Act for consolidating, in One Act, certain " Provisions usually inserted in Acts of Inclosure, and " for facilitating the Mode of proving the several Fasts " usually required on the passing of such Bills," unless the Committee, to whom the Petition or Bill for such Inclosure or Improvement shall be referred, shall otherwise order.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Committee, to whom any Petition or Bill for the inclosing any Lands or Grounds, or for extinguishing any Right of Common thereon, shall be referred, may admit Proof of the Notices required by the Standing Orders of this House, and of the Allegations in the Preamble of such Bill, by Affidavit taken and authenticated according to the Form prescribed in the Schedule to the said Bill, unless such Committee shall otherwise order.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Three last Resolutions shall not take Effect, unless the said Bill shall pass into a Law.

The said Resolutions being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That the said Resolutions be made Standing Orders of this House.

Ordered, That the said Resolutions be printed.

And then the House adjourned till Thursday Morning next. Ten of the Clock.

And afterwards a Speech of the Lords Commissioners was delivered to both Houses by the Lord High Chancellor; which is as followed!; viz.

My Lords and Gentlemen,

We have it in Command from His Majesty to acquaint you, that, on account of the advanced Period of the Season, and the State of Public Business, He is induced to relieve you from a longer Attendance in Parliament.

His Majesty highly commends the Wisdom, Temper,

and Diligence, which have' marked all your Proceedings; and particularly acknowledges the Assiduity and Zeal with which you have pursued the Investigation of the important Subjects brought under your Consideration, in consequence of the severe Pressure occasioned by the High Price of Corn, The beneficial Effects of the Measures you have suggested for the Alleviation of this Calamity, have afforded His Majesty great Consolation; and He has the utmost Satisfaction in indulging the Hope, that, under the Favour of Providence, the Blefiings of Plenty will be restored by the Produce of the ensuing Harvest.

Gentlemen of the House of Commons,

His Majesty has directed us to return you His particular Thanks for the liberal Provision which you have made for the various Branches of the Public Service. While He regrets the Necessity of Supplies so large, it is a Relief to His Majesty to observe, that the Resources and continued Prolperity of the Country have enabled you to distribute the Public Burthens in such a Manner as to press with as little Severity as possible on His faithful Subjects.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

The brilliant and repeated Successes of His Majesty's Arms by Sea and Land, important as they are in their immediate Consequences, are not less satisfactory to His Majesty's Mind, as affording fresh and decisive Proofs of that vigorous Exertion, undaunted Valour, and steady Perseverance, which distinguish the National Character, and on which the chief Reliance must be placed for Respect Abroad, and for Confidence and Security at Home. Events so honourable to the British Name derive, at the present Moment, peculiar Value in His Majesty's Estimation, from their Tendency to facilitate the Attainment of the great Object of His unceasing Solicitude, the Restoration of Peace on fair and adequate Terms. They furnish at the same Time an additional Pledge, that if the Sentiments of Moderation and Justice which will ever govern His Majesty's Conduct, should be rendered unavailing in this Instance, by unrealonable Pretensions on the Part of His Enemies, the Spirit and Firmness of His People will continue to be manifested by such Efforts and Sacrifices, as may be necessary for averting the Honour of His Majesty's Crown, and for maintaining the permanent Interests of the Empire.

After which a Commission was read, for proroguing the Parliament until Thursday the 6th Day of August next: And the Parliament was accordingly prorogued until Thursday the 6th Day of August next.

Mr. Speaker having, in pursuance of an Act, passed in the 24th Year of the Reign of, His present Majesty, made his Appointment of Members of the House of Commons for the issuing Warrants to the Clerk of the Crown, in the Cafes therein mentioned, the same is here entered, in pursuance of the Directions of the said Act; and is as follows:

theDifcontlnUance of the Receipt of New Years Gifts, my Lords

My Lords having lately under their View the Salaries of the Secretaries of several of the principal Departments, and being sensible that the Business of this Office is much increased, are pleased to take into Confide ration the Salaries of the Secretaries of this Board. For the Purpose of ascertaining with as much Precision as possible the Extent of the Increase of the Business of the Office, my Lords are pleased to c^ll for an Account of the Number of Papers registered for the Consideration of the Board, in the following Periods, which appears to be as follow:

Number of Papers,

It appears also, that the Number of Papers registered for the Consideration of the Board, in 1783, was 2,982; but no regular Register having been kept prior to that Period, their Number in former Years cannot be so precisely Hated: but it is evident from the Books of the Office, that in the Years 1780, 1781, and 1782, they did not exceed the Number registered in 1783.

Read Minute of the 30th November 1782, by which it appears from Accounts then laid before the Board, that the Emoluments of each of the Secretaries, for Three Years of Peace, from 1769 to 1771 inciufive, amounted to £.3,414 per Annum; and for Three Years of War, from 1779 to 1781, inciufive, to £. 5,114 per Annum; and the Emoluments of each of the Chief Clerks for the former Period to £. 853 per Annum; and in the latter Period to £. 1,278: And it appears also by the said Minute, that my Lords were pleased to £x the Salary of each of the Secretaries at £. 3,000 per Annum, and of each of the Chief Clerks at £. 800 per Annum, being nearly One Fourth the relative Proportion received by the Secretaries and Chief Clerks, according to the ancient Distribution of Fees.

My Lords also call for an Account of the only other Emoluments received by the Secretaries and Chief Clerks, in the Year 17825 by which it appears, that in addition to the above Salaries, each of the Secretaries received for New Years Gifts, the Sum of £. 397. 15 s. and each of the Chief Clerks £.99. 8/.

Read also Minute of the 10th October 1797; ^y which it appears, that the Select Committee of the House of Commons, appointed to consider Matters of Finance, having recommended

were pleased to order the Discontinuance of their Receipt; and that a Compensation equal to their Amount should be nude to the Chief Clerks, and other Clerks in the Office, in Lieu thereof.

Read also Minute of the 5th July 1798; by which it appears, in consequence of the very great Increase of the Business in the Office, my Lords are pleased to augment the Salaries of the Chief Clerks, from £.800 to-£.1,000 per Annum, exclusive of the Sum received by them in Lieu of New Years Gifts; and they were also pleased to increase the Salaries of the other Clerks in the Office, in proportion to their Trust and Labour.

My Lords having attentively considered the present State of the Office, the great Increase of Business, and the consequent increased Labour and Responsibility of the Secretaries, in the various Duties of their Situation; and considering also, that the Emoluments, in consequence of the Suppression of New Years Gifts, are less now than they wire in 1782, notwithstanding the additional Business of the Office, are of Opinion, that it is just that an Augmentation should be made to the Salaries of the Secretaries of this Board; and their Lordships are pleased to determine, that the Salary of each of the Secretaries of this Board, shall be fixed at £.4,000 per Annum, to commence from §th January 1800.

On the preceding Minute being read, Mr. Rose, one of the Joint Secretaries, expressed to the Board his Determination not to avail himself of the liberal Attention of my Lords to the Secretaries, to the Extent intended by their Lordships; being in Possession of another Employment of considerable Value, which does not require his Attendance, he states it to be inconsistent with his Feelings to allow himself to be placed in ,a better Situation as Secretary to this Board than under the Arrangement made in 1782, when the Income of his then Colleague and himself was fixed at less than Two-Thirds of what they were previous thereto in Possession of; and much lower-dun the preceding Peace Average; Mr. Rose desiring only to receive an Indemnification for the New Years picts, according to their reduced Amount, when they were flopped in consequence of the Report of the Finance Committee alluded to in the Minute, which will leave him with an Increase less by about £. 150 a Year than under the Settlement in 1782.

My Lords arc pleased to approve of this Waivor of Mr. Rose being entered on the Minutes, and of his receiving an Indemnification for the New Years Gifts, as reduced, to commence from the Year 1797, the Period to which the same appear to have been received.

This Arrangement was made in Consideration of the Alteration which has taken place in this Office, in consequence of Two Acts of Parliament, the one passed in 1794, for the better Management of the Land Revenue, the other passed in 1798, for the Sale of Parts of the Estates of the Crown, in order to provide a Fund for the Purchase of the Land Tax, payable out of the Crown Lands; by means of which Acts, the Business of the Office has been

dintini&edL

Annum 1 fer that the Addition or Compensation for the increased Bufrness h, on an Average, equal to £.466. i8x. tod.i but the Salaries and Office Fees for the lad Year having amounted only to £. 1,114. 4s. 11 d. the Compensation for that Year was £.885. 15/. id.

RECEIVER OF THE ONE SHILLING AND SIXPENNY DUTIES.

SIR,

Upper Eaton Street, Grosvenor Place, February 10th 1801.

In obedience to the Commands of the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty's Treasury, communicated to me in your Letter of the 7th Instant, I have the Honour to inform you, that upon the Consolidation of the Offices of Receiver of the 1 /. and 6d. Duties, which took place in July last, the Poundage of 3 d. per Pound, heretofore paid on each Duty, was reduced to t d. \ per Pound; and by the Calculation which was then made, it appeared that this reduced Rate of Poundage on the probable future Annual Amount of both Duties, taken upon an Average of the lad Seven Years Receipt, would give me £. 94, 8 /. 6 d. Increase of Poundage. — Out of which Sum all Expences whatever, for Clerks, Stationary, and Postage of Letters, attending the Management of both Duties, are to be paid; also the Charge of employing an Agent at Edinburgh for receiving and remitting the Sixpenny Duty from Scotland; besides the casual Expence of passing a Privy Seal and giving new Security.

1 have the Honour to be.

SIR,

Your obedient humble Servant,

John Lane,

Receiver of the One Shilling and Sixpenny Duties on Salaries and Pensions.

Charles Long, Esq.

Secretary Treasury, See. Scc. &c.

THIS Account is properly stated and vouched. The Superin- tendent Magistrate was examined upon Oath; he declared, that the Account is just and true in every Particular. The Number of the Watchmen is regularly kept full with efficient Men, agreeable to the Augmentation of the last Year, which has necessarily increased the Expence very considerably. The Licences to Pawnbrokers, which have been raised from Ten to an Hundred Pounds each, have been very productive, as many have continued at the high Licence to get off their Goods on Hand. The Estimate of last Year was, that Thirty Persons would take out Licences at an Hundred Pounds each, whereas Forty-four have done it this Year. It is intended to continue the Augmentation of the Watchmen so long in the Spring as this Surplus Fund shall last. It is probable there will be a considerable Reduction in the Carriage Duty, on account of the high Price of Hay and Oats; however, he considers the Funds will continue sufficient for the Purposes of his Establishment. The late Lord Mayor also declared, that he reviewed the Watchmen a few Days before he went out of Office: the Returns were full, the Men appeared well armed and cloathed: he examined the Constables, who gave him satisfactory Accounts relative to the Men and their Conduct, and the Whole appeared to him to be well appointed, complete in Numbers, and in good Order.

The SEVENTH ACCOUNT of Money expended by the Rive a Boynb Company, in carrying on the Boyne Navigation: from the Twentieth Day of April One thousand Seven hundred and Ninety-five, to the Twenty-seventh Day of December One thousand Seven hundred and Ninety-seven; pursuant to several Acts of Parliament, passed in relation to Inland Navigations.

THIS Account is properly dated, and vouched. The Secretary, Accountant, and Engineer, were examined upon Oath; who declared, the Money was honedly expended, and the Account jud and true. They also declared, that though the Line of the Navigation from Drogheda to Trim, according to the Plan laid before Parliament, in the Year One thousand Seven hundred and Eighty-nine, has not been ftriCMy adhered to in the Execution of the Works, inasmuch as they have deserted the Bed of the River, and made a Still.Water Canal, yet this Deviation from the original Plan was adopted from Motives of Economy, and founded on Experience 5 and by so doing, the Canal will probably be executed, to Trim, Twelve Thousand Pounds under the original Estimate, and be more serviceable, by not being subjetl to Winter Floods, or other Inconveniencies attending a River Navigation; and will also make the Navigation from Drogheda to Trim shorter than by the original Plan.

2 9th April.

Dublin Castle, April 1801.

Mr Lord,

I have received the Honour of your Grace's Letter of the 31st of March, inclosing a Copy of a Resolution of the' House of Commons, requiring an Account of such Places and Offices of Profit under the Crown in Ireland, as are actually held by Members of that House; and desiring that i should give Directions for its being prepared and transmitted as soon as possible.

I beg Leave to observe to your Grace, that we have not any authen-cated Lift of the House of Commons, nor do we receive any Official

Information of the Places and Offices of Profit held by Members returned to that House; I have how ever caused an Account to be made out, agreeably to the Order of the House, from the bell Information that we are possessed of, which I have the Honour to inclose herewith.

I have the Honour to be, with great Truth and Regard, My Lord, Your Grace's

moil obedient humble Servant,

Cor mv allls.

His Grace

I The Duke of Portl a nd, &c. &c. &c.

s

William Irving,

Inspector General of the Imports and Exports of Great Britain.

IN the Year 1697, certain Rates of Value were affixed to the several Articles Imported into and Exported from this Kingdom; and, consonant to these Estimates, the Ledgers of the Inspector General's Office are (till kept, and the Public Accounts are Bated accordingly.

By the Act of the 38th of His Majesty, commonly called The Convoy Act, the Merchants Exporters are required to declare the real Value of British Manufactures exported, in order that the Amount of the Duty chargeable thereon may be ascertained; but the Exports to Ireland, certain Articles used in the Fisheries, and Cotton Manufactures, of all Dcscriptions, being exempted from Payment of this Duty, and consequently from the Declaration of the Exporters, as to the Value, the inspector General therefore cannot make an Ojfiaal Return lo that Part of the Order of the

House, which requires the Difference between the Official Value and the Declared Value.

But assuming, that Articles exported to Ireland, or used in the Fisheries, may beeftimated at the same Rate of Value with Articles of a similar Nature exported to other Countries, and that an Eiti-mate which has with great Pains been formed of the true Value of Cofton Manufactures exported, iscorreft; the Inspector General thinks himself justified in Bating to Parliament, that the Value of British Manufactures exported from Great Br ita'in to all Parts, amounted, in the Year 1799, to 38,942,498, andin the Year i8co, to 39,471,203.

No Account can as yet be prepared of the Value of the lmj oits from India and China, for the Year ending the 5th January lall.

PROPOSAL for the Establishment of A Military College.

THE Necessity of an Establishment for the Indru&ioQ of Officers of the Army, in the higher Duties of their Profession, and of giving to those intended for the Service, such an Education as may best prepare them for the fame, having become evident, sundry Papers have been submitted from Time to Time to those Officers most competent to judge of the Merits of such a Measure, and of the belt Means of carrying it into Effect.

After due Deliberation, and reducing the same to a System, in its Outlet futhciently extensive, confident with the (Economy necessary to be observed, the following Outline of a Plan is submitted to Consideration, proposing to found in this Country an Establishment for the Purpose of Military Indruction: —

The Establishment of a Military College, to consist of — a Senior, and, a Junior Department.

in the Senior Department, shall be admitted Thirty Officers, to be instructed in the Duties of the General Staff of the Army, and in particular those which belong to the Quarter Mailer General in the Field.

The Staff of this Department is contained in Schedule, (No. 1.)

It is proposed that this Edablidiment shall be governed, as a Military Body, according to His Majesty's Rules and Regulations for the Discipline of the Service, with such additional Restrictions at may be necessary to the Conduct of Youth, and the Objects of the Iaftitution.

The Commander in Chief for the Time being, will be Chief Governor of the Military College; under whose Control the Eda-blishment will be placed.

Each Department will be under the Command of Officers of Rank in the Army, who wiM be responsible to the Resident Lieutenant Governor for the Discipline, the Conduct of the Studies, together with the interior Care and (Economy of their respective Departments.

All Elementary Tuition will be conduced by Professors and Maders, subject to the Control of a Director of IndruClion.

Public Examinations will be held of the Progress made by Students in their Studies.

A Board composed of the Senior Officers of the College will hold the Examinations, investigate the Accounts, and transact such other Business belonging to the Inditution, as shall by the Statutes of the College be placed under its Cognizance.

The Junior Department, to be for the Instruction of those who are from early Life intended for a Military Profession, and who will by this Moans be well grounded in a Knowledge of Science, previous to their attaining the Age that enables them to hold Com. millions in the Army.

This Department is proposed to receive Three Hundred Students, from the Ages of Fourteen to Sixteen; of which Number, Fifty may be Cadets of the East India Company's Service; One Hundred, the Sons of Noblemen and Gentlemen, who roa intend them for the Service; One Hundred, the Sons of Officers attually

The Collegiate Board shall report their Proceedings to the Chief Governor, who will lay the same Annually before a Supreme Board, composed cf such*Generais, and other Persons, as His Majesty may think proper to nominate.

The Staff of this Department is contained in Schedule, (No. 2.)

The General Staff of the Military College is contained in Schedule, (No. 3.)

N° 3.

EXTRACT of a Report to His Royal Highnefsthe Commander in Chief, from the Quarter Mailer General and Adjutant General; on the Plan proposed for founding a Mil it a*, r College.

4< IN Obedience to Your Royal HighnefOs Commands, we have Carefully examined and maturely considered the Papers laid before us, containing a Plan for the Establishment of a Royal Military College, together with the Mode to be adopted for carrying the same into Effeft; we have the Honour to make our Report thereon.

rt It is proposed to found the Establishment in Two Departments, making each Division a leparare Course of Study. By thus classing Inflrudion under dirtintt Heads, the Rudiments, as well as the higher Branches of Military Science, may be equally taught, leaving the Individual to purlue that Course which most immediately applies to his own Rank and particular Prospects in the Service.

" Of the Two Departments, the Second is intended as the Basis of a regular Course of Education, and is adapted to those Persons in particular, who are from early Life intended for the Military

Profession.

4i In considering the Interior and Military Regulations of this Department, it appears to us that its Regulations are judicious, and peculiarly calculated to inflil in Youth a high Scnfe of Honour,

founded on religious and moral Principles; that a just Impression of Subordination will ariie from the Discipline of the Department being conducted according to Military Form, and the established Rules of the Service; w:.il;l in Science, the Study of each Branch is carried to the Extent necessary for Military Purposei in general*

«c The First Department is calculated for the Qualification of Officers intended to serve on the General Staff of an Army.

' This Course of Study is adapted only to those Officers, who, by a regular Course of Military Education, have acquired the first Rudiments of Science, and combine with the Experience of Service the Age of Reflexion.

" Weconsider this Department of the utmost Utility and Importance, as embracing that Knowledge of the various Details which relate to the higher Scale of War, and the Application of Science in the Direction of Military Operations; Qbjects most materially connected with the Success of Armies.

44 Such a Course of Instruction is the more necessary to establish, on Account of its being distinct from the Intelligence to be acquired by Regimental Experience; for to the one belongs the Power to execute, and to the other the judgment to direct."

(Signed)

David Dundas. Harry. Calvert.
